prompt: A technician is troubleshooting an all-in-one laser printer that prints a vertical line when making copies and scans.
When users print or receive faxes, the output from the printer is correct.
Which of the following should the technician examine to determine the cause of the issue?
explanation: The vertical line appears only during copying and scanning, not during printing or faxing. This indicates the issue is with the document feeder path, which is used only when scanning or copying documents. The document feeder's rollers or guides would cause a consistent vertical line to appear on the scanned/copied output. Since normal printing and faxing work correctly, the issue is isolated to the input mechanism rather than the imaging drum or corona wire.

why.A: Pickup rollers feed paper from the tray during printing, but the issue doesn't affect printed or faxed output.
why.B: Corona wire issues would affect all imaging processes including printing and faxing, which work correctly here.
why.D: Drum assembly problems would cause defects in all output modes, but printing and faxing are unaffected.

prompt: Which of the following is an advantage of using a hybrid cloud instead of a public cloud?

options.text: Ability to meet data residency requirements
Ability to leverage IaaS and PaaS

answerText: Ability to meet data residency requirements
explanation: A hybrid cloud architecture allows organizations to keep sensitive data on private infrastructure while leveraging public cloud resources, enabling them to meet data residency and regulatory requirements that mandate data remain within specific
geographic regions or under direct organizational control. This is a primary advantage over pure public cloud solutions where all data is hosted on the provider's infrastructure.

why.A: Hybrid cloud typically increases management overhead compared to public cloud due to managing both private and public environments.
why.B: Cross-platform virtualization is not inherently tied to hybrid cloud architecture and can be used in any cloud model.
why.D: Both public and hybrid clouds can leverage IaaS and PaaS; this is not a distinguishing advantage of hybrid cloud.

prompt: A technician is troubleshooting a desktop PC that is plugged into a UPS. The PC loses the system date/time after every power outage.
Which of the following should the technician do to resolve the issue? (Choose two.)
answerText: Repair the backup power source.; Replace the CMOS battery.
explanation: The CMOS battery maintains the system's real-time clock and BIOS settings during power outages. When it fails, the system loses date/time information after each power loss, even with a UPS protecting the system. Additionally, if the UPS backup power source is faulty and not actually providing power to maintain the CMOS battery during outages, the issue persists. Replacing the CMOS battery and repairing the UPS backup power source addresses both potential causes.

why.A: A BIOS update would not restore CMOS battery functionality or fix a depleted battery.
why.B: RAM issues do not affect the system clock; RAM is volatile memory that doesn't store date/time between shutdowns.
why.C: Disabling NTP would prevent automatic time synchronization but wouldn't resolve the underlying CMOS battery failure.
why.F: A surge protector is redundant with a UPS and wouldn't address the clock loss issue after power outages.

prompt: A network administrator must ensure that a printer will still be assigned a specific IP address even if all addresses are depleted.
Which of the following network configuration concepts is this describing?
explanation: A DHCP reservation ensures a specific device receives the same IP address each time it connects to the network, even when the address pool is depleted. This is accomplished by marking specific MAC addresses to always receive predetermined IP addresses outside the normal lease allocation process, guaranteeing the printer always has a consistent IP regardless of overall address availability.

why.A: VLANs segment networks logically but don't guarantee specific IP address assignment to devices.
why.B: A lease is a temporary assignment with an expiration time; it doesn't ensure permanent address retention when the pool is exhausted.
why.D: An exclusion removes addresses from the pool so they won't be assigned, the opposite of what's needed to guarantee a specific address.

prompt: A user is having issues when charging a device with a Lightning cable. The cable is not recognized when it is plugged into the device. This issue is usually resolved by flipping the cable over. This issue does not occur with other devices of the same type.
Which of the following would most likely cause the issue?

options.text: The device needs to be restarted.
The battery may be swelling and needs inspection.
The cable is failing and needs to be replaced.
The charging port is dirty or damaged

answerText: The charging port is dirty or damaged
explanation: Lightning connectors are reversible by design, so the need to flip the cable to establish recognition indicates a physical port problem. The charging port is likely dirty (debris preventing proper contact) or internally damaged (bent or misaligned pins/contacts). Since the issue is specific to this one device and doesn't occur with other identical devices, it's a hardware defect in the port, not the cable itself.

why.A: A restart wouldn't resolve a hardware charging port recognition issue; the port either makes contact or it doesn't.
why.B: A swelling battery would prevent charging entirely, not cause intermittent recognition based on cable orientation.
why.C: If the cable were failing, flipping it wouldn't reliably resolve the issue, and the problem would likely occur with other devices too.

prompt: Which of the following servers is used to collect data and information about events from a network-connected host?
explanation: A Syslog server is specifically designed to collect, aggregate, and store log data and event information from network devices and hosts. It provides centralized logging for monitoring system events, errors, and diagnostic information across the network infrastructure.

why.A: DNS servers translate domain names to IP addresses; they don't collect event data.
why.B: Mail servers handle email transmission and storage, not network event logging.
why.C: Print servers manage printer resources and job queues, not system event collection.

prompt: A technician observes slow startup times on a laptop.
Which of the following is most likely causing the issue?
explanation: Slow startup times are most commonly caused by a failing or aging hard disk drive (HDD). HDDs have mechanical components that degrade over time, resulting in slow read/write operations during the boot process. An SSD would dramatically improve startup times, making HDD replacement the most effective solution for this symptom.

why.B: RAM affects overall system responsiveness and multitasking performance, but insufficient RAM doesn't typically cause slow startup times.
why.C: Network interface card issues would affect network connectivity, not system startup speed.
why.D: BIOS speed doesn't significantly impact overall startup duration; BIOS execution is a small fraction of boot time.

prompt: A customer reports their tablet was recently dropped on the ground. The tablet has a small crack in one corner of the display, and it does not charge when plugged in.
Which of the following should a technician do first?

options.text: Inspect the USB-C port for damage.

answerText: Inspect the USB-C port for damage.
explanation: After a drop, the tablet fails to charge, indicating potential physical damage to the charging port. The USB-C port should be inspected first for debris, bent pins, or internal damage that would prevent proper connection and power transfer. This is the most direct cause of the charging failure and should be examined before attempting repairs that might mask a more serious underlying issue.

why.A: A hard restart won't resolve a hardware charging port issue; the problem is physical, not software.
why.B: Battery replacement is premature before determining if the port itself is damaged and preventing charge detection.
why.D: Digitizer diagnostics address the display's touch functionality, not the charging failure symptom.

prompt: A technician needs to select PC components with a minimal number of visible internal cables.
Which of the following should the technician use?
explanation: A modular power supply allows technicians to connect only the necessary cables, leaving unused cables disconnected and hidden, thereby minimizing visible internal cabling. SATA drives still require visible cables, liquid cooling systems have visible tubes and fittings, and wireless NICs don't address internal cable visibility.

why.A: SATA drives still require visible data and power cables to connect to the motherboard and power supply.
why.B: Liquid cooling systems include visible radiators, tubes, and hoses that add to internal cable clutter.
why.D: A wireless NIC addresses network connectivity, not the number of visible internal cables.

prompt: A user is traveling internationally. They can make and receive phone calls but cannot send or receive email.
Which of the following would most likely resolve this issue?
explanation: Email requires data connectivity, while calling uses voice services. When traveling internationally, data roaming must be explicitly enabled to access cellular data networks needed for email. The user can make calls because voice services may operate differently than data, but email cannot function without active data connectivity.

why.A: Disabling GPS has no effect on email or data connectivity capabilities.
why.C: Configuring 4G usage only doesn't address whether data roaming is enabled; it may actually limit connectivity if 4G isn't available.
why.D: Using a hotspot requires the device to already have data connectivity, which is the underlying problem being addressed.

prompt: Which of the following should be used when installing network cabling above a drop ceiling that is part of the shared air space?
explanation: Plenum-rated cabling is specifically designed for use in plenum spaces—the shared air space above drop ceilings used for ventilation and air circulation. These cables use fire-retardant materials that produce minimal smoke and toxic fumes if they burn, meeting building codes and safety regulations for these critical spaces.

why.A: Shielded twisted pair addresses electromagnetic interference but has no special fire-safety rating for plenum use.
why.C: Optical fiber doesn't require plenum-rating; it's used for long-distance high-speed connections, not typically overhead runs.
why.D: Coaxial cable is rarely used for modern network installations and has no plenum-rating certification.

prompt: While using a computer, a user reports that the system fan begins running loudly and the display starts to distort.
Which of the following is occurring?
explanation: A loudly running fan and display distortion are classic signs of overheating. The system increases fan speed to cool down when internal temperatures rise excessively, and thermal stress causes display artifacts and pixel errors. Both symptoms occurring together point directly to a thermal management problem.

why.B: Sluggish performance alone wouldn't typically cause display distortion or excessive fan noise.
why.C: Overclocking CPU might increase fan speed but doesn't typically cause display distortion unless combined with instability.
why.D: Crashing applications wouldn't cause continuous loud fan operation or display distortion as primary symptoms.

prompt: Which of the following is a common feature of managed switches?
explanation: Port VLAN assignment is a standard feature of managed switches, allowing administrators to assign specific ports to different virtual LANs for network segmentation and traffic control. This is a core management capability that distinguishes managed switches from unmanaged ones.

why.A: Remote device power delivery is not a standard managed switch feature; that's typically a PoE injector capability.
why.C: Content filtering is a firewall or application-layer feature, not a typical managed switch function.
why.D: Load balancing is typically handled by dedicated load balancers or routers, not standard managed switches.

prompt: Which of the following is a characteristic of Type 2 hypervisors?
explanation: Type 2 hypervisors (also called hosted hypervisors) run on top of an existing host operating system and require that OS to function. Unlike Type 1 bare-metal hypervisors, they depend on the underlying OS for hardware access and management.

why.A: Bare-metal installation is a characteristic of Type 1 hypervisors, not Type 2.
why.C: Type 2 hypervisors can support remote management depending on the host OS capabilities.
why.D: Type 2 hypervisors are less demanding hardware-wise than Type 1 since they leverage the host OS.

prompt: Which of the following port numbers is used for a file transfer?
explanation: Port 21 is the standard port number used for FTP (File Transfer Protocol), which is used for transferring files over a network. Port 53 is for DNS, port 68 is for DHCP, and port 389 is for LDAP.

why.B: Port 53 is used for DNS (Domain Name System), not file transfer.
why.C: Port 68 is used for DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol), not file transfer.
why.D: Port 389 is used for LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol), not file transfer.

prompt: A user wants to print files from an overseas office using a shared network folder The user's laptop has no public-facing internet connectivity.
Which of the following can be used to print from the shared network folder?
explanation: SMB (Server Message Block) is the protocol used for accessing shared network folders and printing to network printers on Windows networks. Since the user needs to print from a shared network folder without public internet, SMB provides the necessary file sharing and print service functionality across the local network infrastructure.

why.A: ADF (Automatic Document Feeder) is a scanner hardware component, not a printing or network protocol.
why.B: USB is a physical connection method and doesn't enable printing from a remote shared network folder.
why.C: PCL (Printer Command Language) is a printer language for formatting print jobs, not a network file or print sharing protocol.

prompt: A user tries to connect a monitor to a laptop to have an additional screen for work, but both screens show the same content.
Which of the following should the user do to resolve the issue?

options.text: Use the Add New Hardware assistant to add the monitor and set up the required settings.
Purchase a docking station to connect both the laptop and the monitor.
Configure the Windows tiling feature to display multiple windows.
Go to the Display settings and configure the external monitor as extended.

answerText: Go to the Display settings and configure the external
explanation: monitor as extended.

When a monitor shows the same content as the laptop screen, it's configured in mirror/duplicate mode rather than extended mode. To use the monitor as an additional screen, the user must access Windows Display settings and configure the external monitor as an extended display, which will allow them to use both screens for different content simultaneously.

why.A: Hardware assistants are not needed for modern monitors; display configuration is handled through OS settings.
why.B: A docking station is not required to resolve this issue; the monitor is already connected and recognized.
why.C: Windows tiling arranges windows on existing displays but does not change the display mode from mirrored to extended.

prompt: Which of the following best represents the purpose of NFC?

options.text: Short-distance wireless connections between two devices
Wireless connections between multiple devices at once
Direct connection of two computers for file sharing

explanation: devices

NFC (Near Field Communication) is specifically designed for short-distance wireless communication, typically within a few centimeters, between two devices. It enables quick data exchange between compatible devices without requiring pairing or complex setup, making it ideal for contactless payments and device communication.

why.A: NFC is wireless, not wired.
why.C: NFC communicates between two devices, not multiple devices simultaneously.
why.D: While NFC can facilitate file sharing, it is not limited to direct computer connections and serves many other purposes.

prompt: A group of friends is gathering in a room to play video games. One of the friends has a game server.
Which of the following network types should the group use so they can all connect to the same server and the internet?
explanation: A LAN (Local Area Network) is the appropriate network type for a group of devices in a single physical location, such as a room. A LAN allows multiple computers to connect to the same server and share internet access within a limited geographic area, making it ideal for friends in a room playing video games together.

why.A: A SAN (Storage Area Network) is specialized for storage device connectivity, not general gaming or internet access.
why.B: A MAN (Metropolitan Area Network) covers a larger geographic area than a room, such as a city or campus.
why.D: A PAN (Personal Area Network) is extremely limited in range and connects only a few personal devices, not suitable for multiple users in a room.

prompt: Which of the following can a user utilize to share their mobile phone connection with their laptop?
explanation: Tethering is the process of sharing a mobile phone's internet connection with other devices such as a laptop. It allows the phone to act as a mobile hotspot, enabling connected devices to access the internet through the phone's cellular connection.

why.A: IR (Infrared) is used for short-distance control and communication, not for sharing internet connections.
why.B: NFC is designed for very short-distance data exchange, not for sustained internet connection sharing.
why.C: Wi-Fi Direct allows direct peer-to-peer connections between devices but is not the primary method for sharing cellular internet.

prompt: A user reports that their desktop PC does not turn on.
Which of the following components would most likely cause the issue?
explanation: The Power Supply Unit (PSU) is the most likely component to cause a complete system failure where the desktop PC does not turn on at all. If the PSU fails, no power is delivered to any component, preventing the entire system from starting. Without power, the system cannot reach POST or any operational state.

why.B: A failed GPU would not prevent the system from powering on; it would either not display video or fail after POST.
why.C: Faulty RAM would cause POST failures or system hangs, but the system would still power on.
why.D: A failed CPU would prevent POST completion, but the system would still attempt to power on and may show signs of trying to start.

prompt: The printer in a main office repeatedly jams.
Which of the following tasks should a support technician do to solve the issue?
explanation: Repeated paper jams in a printer typically indicate worn or damaged internal components such as pickup rollers, separation pads, or feed mechanisms. A maintenance kit includes replacement parts for these wear-prone components and is the appropriate solution to resolve chronic jamming issues.

why.B: Replacing toner or ink cartridges addresses printing quality or output issues, not mechanical jamming problems.
why.C: Installing a new ribbon is relevant only to impact printers, not modern office printers that jam due to mechanical wear.
why.D: Changing the printhead addresses print quality defects, not paper feed or jamming issues.

prompt: A technician is installing a new printer. After registering the printer, the technician receives an email from the manufacturer stating there is a security vulnerability that can be remediated.
Which of the following steps should the technician take next?

options.text: Disable the default gateway on the printer.

explanation: When a manufacturer identifies a security vulnerability and provides notification, the appropriate remediation step is to update the printer's firmware. Firmware updates patch security vulnerabilities and should be applied promptly to protect the device from exploitation and maintain network security.

why.A: Disabling wireless connectivity is an overly restrictive workaround that limits functionality rather than fixing the underlying vulnerability.
why.B: Enabling audit logging helps monitor activity but does not remediate the actual security vulnerability.
why.D: Disabling the default gateway is not a standard remediation for printer vulnerabilities and would impair device functionality.

prompt: A technician has built a new computer. On the initial startup, the computer passes POST but will not turn on the operating system.
Which of the following components has failed?
explanation: When a computer passes POST (Power-On Self-Test) but fails to boot the operating

system, the issue is with storage/boot devices rather than core hardware like the CPU or power supply. The HDD (or storage device) is the most likely culprit, as POST checks basic hardware but does not verify the OS can be loaded from storage.

why.A: An audio card failure would not prevent the operating system from booting.
why.B: A CPU failure would prevent the system from passing POST successfully.
why.C: A power supply failure would prevent POST from completing; the system would not power on at all.

prompt: A user reports slow internet browsing. The technician finds high CPU and memory usage, and pop-ups occur every minute.
Which of the following should the technician do next?

options.text: Escalate to the network team to check end-to-end connectivity.
Download and install the latest drivers.
Update the anti-malware signatures and scan the system.
Check the wireless settings and validate the DHCP configuration.

answerText: Update the anti-malware signatures and scan the
explanation: system.

The symptoms described—high CPU/memory usage and frequent pop-ups—are classic indicators of malware infection rather than network or driver issues. Updating anti-malware signatures and performing a system scan is the appropriate next step to identify and remove any malicious software causing these resource-intensive symptoms.

why.A: Network connectivity issues would not cause high local CPU/memory usage or pop-ups.
why.B: Driver updates are unrelated to the malware symptoms being exhibited.
why.D: DHCP and wireless settings would not cause the specific symptoms of malware activity like pop-ups and excessive resource consumption.

prompt: Which of the following is the best to use when testing a file for potential malware?
explanation: A sandbox is an isolated testing environment specifically designed to safely execute and analyze potentially malicious files without risking the host system or network. It allows technicians to observe malware behavior in a controlled, contained space.

why.A: Multitenancy refers to sharing infrastructure among multiple users/organizations and is unrelated to malware testing.
why.B: Test development is a software development practice, not a method for testing potentially malicious files.
why.C: Cross-platform virtualization allows running different operating systems but is not specifically designed for safe malware analysis.

prompt: Which of the following resolutions is commonly known as Ultra HD?
explanation: 3840x2160 is the standard resolution for Ultra HD (UHD) or 4K displays. It represents four times the pixel count of 1080p and is the widely adopted consumer and professional standard for ultra-high-definition content.

why.A: 1920x1080 is Full HD, not Ultra HD.
why.B: 2048x1080 is a cinema-specific resolution, not a standard Ultra HD format.
why.D: 7680x4320 is 8K resolution, which exceeds Ultra HD specifications.

prompt: A technician is troubleshooting stylus issues on identical company-provided tablets. Users can purchase their own accessories. Some users have no issues, but others report that their styluses charge intermittently and die frequently.
Which of the following is the most likely cause of this issue?

options.text: Certain cases are causing charging issues.
The tablets need to be updated.
Some of the tablets have manufacturing defects.
The malfunctioning styluses need firmware updates.

answerText: Certain cases are causing charging issues.
explanation: Since identical tablets show different stylus charging issues and users purchase their own accessories, the problem is most likely caused by third-party cases that interfere with the stylus charging contacts or mechanism. This explains why some users with different cases experience problems while others with compatible cases do not.

why.B: If tablets needed updating, all identical tablets would exhibit the same issue.
why.C: Manufacturing defects would affect the tablets themselves, not specifically the styluses, and would be consistent across identical units.
why.D: Firmware updates on styluses would not explain why identical styluses work for some users but not others.

prompt: A user prints a job from a laser printer. The user wipes the page, and the words and images come off of it. The technician replaces the toner cartridge, but the issue persists.
Which of the following components should the technician replace next?
explanation: Toner coming off the page when wiped indicates a fusing problem. The fuser applies heat and pressure to permanently bond toner to paper. If toner doesn't adhere properly, the fuser is malfunctioning and should be replaced next. Since replacing the toner cartridge didn't resolve the issue, the problem is with the fuser mechanism, not the toner supply.

why.B: A faulty drum would cause image quality issues but would not result in toner wiping off after printing.
why.C: Developer roller problems would affect toner distribution and image quality, not toner adhesion to paper.
why.D: A discharge lamp issue would affect image formation and contrast, not toner permanence on the page.

prompt: Which of the following has the best penetration through physical objects, such as walls?
explanation: The 2.4GHz frequency has longer wavelengths than 5GHz and 6GHz, which allows it to penetrate physical obstacles like walls more effectively. Lower frequency signals generally have better propagation through solid objects, making 2.4GHz the best choice for wall penetration among wireless standards.

why.B: 5GHz has shorter wavelengths and higher frequency, resulting in poorer wall penetration compared to 2.4GHz.
why.C: 6GHz is even higher frequency than 5GHz and provides even worse penetration through physical objects.
why.D: NFC (Near Field Communication) is a close-range technology designed for short distances and does not penetrate walls effectively.

prompt: Which of the following is a Bluetooth network an example of?
explanation: Bluetooth is a wireless personal area network (PAN) technology that connects devices over short distances (typically up to 10-100 meters). PANs are designed for interconnecting personal devices in a limited area, which is exactly what Bluetooth accomplishes.

why.B: LAN (Local Area Network) typically covers a larger area like an office or building and uses different technologies.
why.C: WAN (Wide Area Network) covers much larger geographic distances and is not appropriate for Bluetooth's short-range design.
why.D: SAN (Storage Area Network) is specifically for storage device connectivity and is unrelated to Bluetooth technology.

prompt: Which of the following cloud models would multiple organizations in the same industry most likely use?
explanation: A community cloud is shared among multiple organizations with common interests, concerns, or missions—such as those in the same industry. This model allows organizations to share infrastructure and resources while maintaining separation from the general public cloud and other industries.

why.A: A public cloud is open to all users and not specific to organizations within a particular industry.
why.B: A hybrid cloud combines public and private clouds but is not specifically designed for industry-specific organizational sharing.
why.D: A private cloud is dedicated to a single organization and would not be shared among multiple companies in the same industry.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of VDI?

options.text: Streaming a GUI to thin clients from a server
Provisioning a sandbox as a test environment
Providing high-performance workstations with a local OS
Launching a virtual machine server on a hypervisor

answerText: Streaming a GUI to thin clients from a server
explanation: VDI (Virtual Desktop Infrastructure) is defined as streaming a graphical user interface to thin clients from a centralized server. This allows users to access their desktop environment remotely while the actual processing and storage occurs on the server. Option A correctly describes this architecture where the GUI is rendered and transmitted
to lightweight client devices.

why.B: Provisioning a sandbox is a testing/isolation technique unrelated to VDI desktop delivery.
why.C: High-performance workstations with local OS represent traditional computing, not VDI which centralizes resources.
why.D: Launching a virtual machine on a hypervisor describes virtualization but not specifically VDI desktop infrastructure.

prompt: A company needs to develop a disaster recovery solution based on virtual machines.
Which of the following service models is the most suitable?
explanation: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) is the most suitable model for a disaster recovery solution based on virtual machines because it provides on-demand access to computing resources, storage, and networking infrastructure. Organizations can provision virtual machines, replicate data, and maintain failover capabilities without owning physical infrastructure. IaaS gives the control and flexibility needed for DR planning.

why.B: Security as a Service focuses on security controls and threat protection, not infrastructure provisioning for DR.
why.C: Platform as a Service provides development frameworks and middleware, not the infrastructure-level control needed for VM-based disaster recovery.
why.D: Software as a Service delivers applications to end-users, not the underlying infrastructure required for disaster recovery solutions.

prompt: A technician is connecting a hands-free car system via Bluetooth.
Which of the following is a security feature that should be used for this task?
explanation: A PIN code is the appropriate security feature for pairing a hands-free car system via Bluetooth. PIN codes (typically 4-6 digits) are used during the initial Bluetooth pairing process to authenticate and establish a secure connection between devices. This prevents unauthorized devices from pairing with the car system.

why.A: BitLocker is a Windows full-disk encryption technology, not a Bluetooth pairing security mechanism.
why.B: Biometrics (fingerprint, facial recognition) are not standard Bluetooth security features for initial pairing.
why.C: TPM (Trusted Platform Module) is a hardware security chip for local device encryption and attestation, not Bluetooth authentication.

prompt: A technician is troubleshooting a laptop's connectivity via its USB-C port to a projector. The same laptop works well when it is connected to a USB-C docking station. The projector is configured as expected, and the USB-C cable was tested on a charging port.
Which of the following could be the issue?

options.text: The USB-C cable requires a power injector
The USB-C cable is not compatible with Thunderbolt technology.
The USB-C cable needs an adapter to work with the laptop.
The USB-C cable does not support enough power.

answerText: The USB-C cable is not compatible with Thunderbolt
explanation: technology.

The USB-C cable is not compatible with Thunderbolt technology, which is the most likely issue. The laptop works with a USB-C docking station (which may be designed to work with standard USB-C or may have built-in adapters), but the projector requires Thunderbolt support. USB-C is a connector type, while Thunderbolt is a protocol standard. A Thunderbolt 3 or 4 port appears as USB-C physically but requires Thunderbolt-certified cables and devices for proper functionality.

why.A: Power injectors are not relevant to video/data connectivity issues with projectors.
why.C: An adapter would not solve a fundamental protocol incompatibility between USB-C and Thunderbolt standards.
why.D: Power delivery is not the issue since the same cable works fine for charging, indicating adequate power transmission capability.

prompt: A high-end workstation with a RAID 5 array is exhibiting slow data access speeds and occasional errors when retrieving files. The technician investigates further and notices one of the hard drives in the RAID array has an amber light.
Which of the following steps should the technician take to troubleshoot and resolve the issues?

options.text: Review network issues that might be causing slow speeds.
Upgrade all RAID drives to higher capacity models to increase data access speeds.
Replace the failing drive, and then allow the RAID controller to rebuild the array.
Reformat all drives in the RAID array to clear any software issues that might be causing the errors.

answerText: Replace the failing drive, and then allow the RAID
explanation: controller to rebuild the array.

When a drive in a RAID 5 array shows an amber light, this indicates a failing or failed drive. The correct procedure is to replace the failing drive and allow the RAID controller to rebuild the array using the parity information stored across the remaining drives. RAID 5 can tolerate one drive failure, and the rebuild process will restore full redundancy and resolve both the slow speeds and errors caused by the degraded array state.

why.A: Network issues would not cause hard drive indicator lights to turn amber or directly cause file retrieval errors from the RAID array.
why.B: Upgrading all drives is unnecessary and wasteful; only the failing drive needs replacement, and higher capacity does not address the current failure.
why.D: Reformatting all drives would destroy data and is inappropriate; the RAID controller is designed to recover from single drive failures automatically.

prompt: Which of the following provides electricity to devices through network cables?
explanation: A PoE (Power over Ethernet) switch provides electricity to devices through network cables. PoE switches inject DC power onto standard Ethernet cables, allowing connected devices such as IP cameras, wireless access points, and VoIP phones to receive both data and power from a single cable connection, eliminating the need for separate power supplies.

why.A: An edge router routes network traffic but does not provide power delivery through network cables.
why.C: An access point provides wireless connectivity but does not inherently deliver power through network cables unless it is a PoE-powered device itself.
why.D: A patch panel is a passive connectivity device for organizing and terminating network cables; it does not provide electrical power.

prompt: An IT specialist sets up a wireless router in a SOHO environment. Afterward, several devices cannot access the internet and are assigned IP addresses starting with 169.254.
Which of the following is the best action to resolve this issue?
explanation: Devices assigned IP addresses starting with 169.254 are using APIPA (Automatic Private IP Addressing), which occurs when DHCP fails to assign addresses. Rebooting the wireless router will restart the DHCP service, allowing it to properly detect and configure connected devices with valid IP addresses from the DHCP pool. This is the quickest and most direct troubleshooting step for DHCP failures in a SOHO environment.

why.B: Shortening the lease time does not address the root cause of DHCP failure; devices still need DHCP to respond initially.
why.C: Using static IP addresses bypasses DHCP but is impractical in a SOHO environment with multiple dynamic devices and does not fix the underlying router issue.
why.D: Increasing the DHCP pool size is irrelevant if the DHCP service itself is not responding; the pool size is not the problem.

prompt: A customer reports slow network speeds.
Which of the following components is most likely failing?
explanation: A Network Interface Card (NIC) failure is the most likely cause of slow network speeds. The NIC is the hardware component directly responsible for network communication. A failing NIC can cause reduced throughput, packet loss, and connection instability. While CPU, HDD, or RAM issues can impact overall system performance, a NIC failure specifically and directly affects network speed.

why.A: CPU issues typically cause slow system performance overall, not specifically slow network speeds.
why.C: HDD failure would cause slow disk access and file operations, not network speed problems.
why.D: RAM failure would result in system crashes, slowdowns, or errors, but not specifically slow network connectivity.

prompt: A support technician receives a call stating that a user has added a device to the network. The user used the same configurations from another workstation.
When both workstations are turned on, neither can access the network reliably.
Which of the following is the most likely cause of the issue?

options.text: The new computer has a duplicate IP address.
The DNS server is registering both hostnames.
The network cable was improperly terminated
The security on the switchport needs to be reset.

answerText: The new computer has a duplicate IP address.
explanation: When a user copies configurations from an existing workstation to a new device without modification, both machines will have identical IP addresses. This creates an IP address
conflict, causing both devices to experience unreliable network connectivity as the network switches between the two machines with the same address. This is a classic duplicate IP scenario.

why.B: DNS registering both hostnames would not prevent network access; it would simply create duplicate DNS entries.
why.C: An improperly terminated cable would affect only that cable's connectivity, not cause issues with both devices when turned on.
why.D: Switchport security settings would typically block or restrict a port, not cause connectivity issues for both devices simultaneously.

prompt: A technician needs to confirm that desktop PCs can be deployed to a global, remote workforce.
Which of the following specifications should the technician validate?
explanation: When deploying desktop PCs to a global, remote workforce, the technician must validate input voltage specifications because different countries use different electrical standards (110-120V vs 220-240V). Confirming compatible input voltage is critical to ensure the equipment will function safely and reliably across all deployment locations worldwide.

why.B: BIOS language support is a minor localization feature, not a critical specification for global deployment viability.
why.C: Supply chain security relates to procurement and product integrity, not to confirming deployment capability to a remote workforce.
why.D: While power efficiency is a consideration, it is not the primary specification needed to validate deployment capability across different electrical systems.

prompt: A company deploys server machines in a public cloud.
Which of the following cloud service models is this an example of?
explanation: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) is the cloud service model where the provider delivers virtualized computing resources over the internet, including servers, storage, and networking. When a company deploys server machines in a public cloud, they are utilizing IaaS as they are renting and managing virtual server infrastructure rather than purchasing physical hardware.

why.A: Platform as a Service provides development environments and tools, not raw server infrastructure for deployment.
why.B: Anything as a Service is not a standard cloud service model classification.
why.D: Software as a Service delivers applications to end users, not server infrastructure for deploying company applications.

prompt: A customer needs to install a new printer in their network. The customer reports that users had intermittent connectivity issues with previous printers.
Which of the following should the technician configure on the new printer to prevent this issue?
explanation: Intermittent connectivity issues with previous printers indicate that IP address changes or DHCP lease expirations were causing devices to lose connectivity. Assigning a static IP address to the printer ensures its IP address remains constant, preventing the connectivity drops caused by dynamic IP reassignment or lease renewal conflicts.

why.A: Configuring a gateway IP address is necessary for routing but does not prevent intermittent connectivity issues.
why.B: Using DHCP would perpetuate the same problem that caused intermittent connectivity with previous printers.
why.D: A public IP address is unnecessary for internal network printers and does not address the connectivity stability issue.

prompt: Which of the following DNS records would an administrator change to redirect email flow?
explanation: The MX (Mail Exchange) record is the DNS record type that specifies mail servers and prioritizes email delivery to the correct mail server. To redirect email flow to different mail servers or change email routing, an administrator must modify the MX records.

why.B: TXT records store text information for various purposes like verification but do not control email flow routing.
why.C: SPF records specify which servers are authorized to send email but do not redirect email flow themselves.
why.D: CNAME records create aliases for domain names but are not used to redirect email flow to different mail servers.

prompt: A technician is troubleshooting a network issue. Users report that the connection keeps dropping and reconnecting every few seconds. The technician:

Verifies the network configuration settings are correct on the workstation Tests the network cable from the workstation to the switch and finds no issues Uses a known-good workstation on the existing network cable and replicates the reported issue
Which of the following should the technician do next?

options.text: Add new network hardware to reduce congestion
Assign a static IP to the impacted workstations.
Validate the environment for external interference.
Check the network logs for evidence of port flapping.

answerText: Check the network logs for evidence of port flapping.
explanation: The technician has already verified configuration settings, tested the physical cable, and replicated the issue with a known-good workstation on the same cable. This indicates the problem is with the network infrastructure itself. Checking network logs for port flapping would reveal if the switch port is rapidly cycling up and down, which would explain the dropping and reconnecting behavior observed by users.

why.A: Adding new hardware would not address the root cause and is premature without identifying the actual problem.
why.B: Static IP assignment would not resolve a physical layer or switch port issue causing intermittent connectivity.
why.C: While interference could cause issues, the fact that a known-good workstation replicated the problem on the same cable points to the switch port as the source.

prompt: Which of the following would prevent a virtual machine from communicating with any endpoints on a network or the internet?
explanation: A sandbox is an isolated computing environment designed to restrict a virtual machine's access to network resources and external systems. By definition, sandboxing prevents a VM from communicating with endpoints on the network or the internet, as this isolation is the primary purpose of the sandbox environment.

why.A: VDI (Virtual Desktop Infrastructure) is a deployment method that still allows network communication.
why.B: A private cloud still allows internal network communication between resources.
why.D: A Type 1 hypervisor is just the underlying virtualization layer and does not inherently prevent network communication.

prompt: A technician recently updated the firmware on a dual-BIOS motherboard. Following the update, the system has been stuck in a boot loop and cannot start an OS from any internal or external device. The technician cannot access the UEFI menu either.
Which of the following should the technician do next?

options.text: Start a warranty repair of the motherboard.
Reapply thermal paste to the CPU.

explanation: A dual-BIOS motherboard has a primary and secondary BIOS chip specifically designed for recovery scenarios. When a firmware update fails and corrupts the primary BIOS to the point where the UEFI menu is inaccessible and the system cannot boot, enabling the secondary BIOS configuration is the recovery method built into the motherboard design to restore functionality.

why.B: Downgrading firmware via USB would require accessing the UEFI menu or a recovery interface, which is not available in this scenario.
why.C: Warranty repair is premature when a dual-BIOS motherboard's recovery feature is available and designed for exactly this situation.
why.D: Reapplying thermal paste has no relevance to a firmware corruption issue and would not resolve the boot loop problem.

prompt: Which of the following cloud models exclusively utilizes a local data center?
explanation: A private cloud model exclusively utilizes a local data center owned and operated by the organization. It provides dedicated infrastructure for a single customer with complete control over data and security. Public clouds use shared infrastructure managed by third parties, hybrid clouds combine both private and public elements, and community clouds serve specific groups but may not be entirely local.

why.B: Public clouds use shared infrastructure managed by third-party providers, not local data centers.
why.C: Hybrid clouds combine both private and public cloud resources, not exclusively local.
why.D: Community clouds serve multiple organizations but are not exclusively limited to a single local data center.

prompt: A customer has several bare-metal servers running a mix of Windows, Linux, and Unix OSs. The customer wants to consolidate the servers but is concerned about data privacy and recurring costs.
Which of the following solutions should a technician recommend?
explanation: A Type 2 hypervisor (hosted hypervisor) runs on top of an existing operating system and allows the customer to consolidate multiple bare-metal servers onto virtualized machines while maintaining control over the hardware in their own data center. This addresses both the privacy concern (data stays on-premises) and cost concerns (reducing physical hardware). IaaS would require external hosting, containers don't fully address OS compatibility for Windows/Unix/Linux mixes, and VDI is for desktop virtualization, not server consolidation.

why.A: IaaS would host infrastructure externally, raising data privacy concerns for a cost-conscious customer.
why.B: Containers require containerized applications and don't effectively handle disparate OS requirements like Windows, Linux, and Unix.
why.D: VDI (Virtual Desktop Infrastructure) is designed for desktop virtualization, not consolidating multiple bare-metal servers.

prompt: A technician is troubleshooting internet connectivity issues after a firewall update. Users report that they can access local network resources, such as printers and shares, but cannot access the internet.
Which of the following settings is most likely causing the issue?
explanation: The default gateway is the critical setting that routes traffic destined for networks outside the local subnet to the internet. If the firewall update misconfigured or blocked the default gateway setting, users can still access local resources (which don't require the gateway) but cannot reach the internet. Static IP assignments, subnet masks, and VLANs would not selectively block only internet access while preserving local network access.

why.A: Static IP assignments alone do not determine internet connectivity; the gateway is what enables external routing.
why.C: An incorrect subnet mask would prevent access to both local and remote networks, not just internet access.
why.D: VLAN configuration affects local network segmentation but would not selectively block only internet while allowing local access.

prompt: A help desk technician inspects a laptop keyboard because a single key has stopped working. The technician checks the keyboard for debris.
Which of the following actions should the technician do next to troubleshoot the issue cost-effectively?
explanation: After checking for debris, the most cost-effective next step is to replace the keycap, which is a simple, inexpensive component that often resolves stuck or non-responsive keys. If the keycap replacement fails, then progression to replacing the key switch (mechanical component) or keyboard assembly would be warranted. Replacing the circuit board or entire keyboard should only occur after simpler fixes are exhausted.

why.A: Replacing the entire keyboard is expensive and premature before attempting simpler fixes like keycap replacement.
why.B: Replacing the key switch is more costly and complex than first attempting a keycap replacement.
why.C: Replacing the circuit board is the most expensive option and should only be considered after all other troubleshooting fails.

prompt: An end user's domain password expires while they are working from home. The end user tries to reset the password using Ctrl+Alt+Delete and then receives the following message:
Configuration information could not be read from the domain controller, either because the machine is unavailable or because access denied.
Which of the following will resolve this issue?

options.text: Reset the account in Active Directory.

explanation: The error message indicates the computer cannot reach the domain controller to process the password change. When working from home, the user's computer is disconnected from the corporate network and cannot communicate with the domain controller. Connecting to the VPN establishes a secure tunnel to the corporate network, allowing the machine to reach the domain controller and complete the password reset. Restarting the computer, resetting the account in Active Directory, or joining Wi-Fi alone would not resolve the connectivity gap to the domain controller.

why.A: Restarting the computer will not resolve the underlying issue of being unable to reach the domain controller.
why.C: Resetting the account in Active Directory requires administrative access and is not the user's responsibility; VPN connectivity is the missing link.
why.D: Simply joining the Wi-Fi network does not provide access to the corporate domain controller unless it is a VPN connection.

prompt: A computer displays an error message indicating there is insufficient storage when installing applications. The user reports slow application load times.
Which of the following replacement components would best resolve this issue?
explanation: The symptoms indicate both storage capacity issues (insufficient storage error) and performance problems (slow load times). An SSD (Solid State Drive) addresses both concerns: it provides fast read/write speeds to eliminate slow application load times and offers adequate storage capacity at reasonable cost. An HDD would only marginally improve speed, USB is external and temporary, and RAM would not resolve storage capacity issues.

why.B: USB storage is external, temporary, and not suitable for installing applications or resolving the underlying storage problem.
why.C: While an HDD provides capacity, it does not significantly improve the slow load times compared to an SSD.
why.D: RAM improves system responsiveness and multitasking but does not resolve storage capacity or provide persistent application load speed improvements.

prompt: A technician is troubleshooting a connectivity issue on a network computer. The technician runs ipconfig in a command prompt and receives the following IP address: 169.254.0.6.
Which of the following is most likely the type of IP address being assigned?
explanation: An IP address in the range 169.254.0.0/16 is an Automatic Private IP Address (APIPA), which is self-assigned by the computer when it cannot reach a DHCP server. This occurs when there is no DHCP server available or the computer cannot communicate with one. DHCP reservations and dynamic assignments would be assigned by a DHCP server, and static assignments are manually configured by an administrator.

why.A: DHCP reservations are assigned by a DHCP server and fall within the configured DHCP pool, not in the APIPA range.
why.B: Dynamic assignments from a DHCP server would fall within the configured DHCP scope, not the 169.254.x.x APIPA range.
why.D: Static assignments are manually configured and would not be in the automatic 169.254.x.x range.

prompt: Which of the following storage options would a technician most likely recommend to have large amounts of affordable capacity without concern for read times on a desktop computer?
explanation: A 2TB SATA 3.5" 5,400rpm HDD offers large affordable capacity at a low cost per gigabyte, making it ideal for users prioritizing storage quantity over read speed. The question explicitly states 'without concern for read times,' so the slower rotational speed is acceptable. The NVMe SSD is much more expensive per GB, the RAID 1 configuration halves usable capacity, and the 15,000rpm SAS drive is enterprise-grade and extremely expensive.

why.A: The 750GB NVMe M.2 SSD is expensive per gigabyte and provides minimal capacity compared to the alternatives.
why.B: RAID 1 mirroring reduces usable capacity to 1TB total and is more costly, defeating the 'affordable capacity' requirement.
why.D: The 4TB SAS 15,000rpm drive is enterprise-grade, extremely expensive per GB, and overkill for a desktop computer's performance needs.

prompt: Which of the following utilizes specialized ports on a laptop to expand the local connection options?
explanation: A docking station utilizes specialized ports on a laptop to expand local connection options by providing additional USB ports, network connections, video outputs, and other peripherals. While a port replicator also expands connections, docking stations are the primary technology designed for this purpose and offer more comprehensive expansion capabilities.

why.A: NFC adapters enable wireless near-field communication but do not expand local connection options.
why.C: Port replicators do expand connections but are less commonly referenced as the standard answer for this function compared to docking stations.
why.D: USB dongles are passive adapters that convert one connector type to another but do not expand the overall number of connection options available.

prompt: Which of the following tools would a technician use to connect wires to an RJ45 connector?
explanation: A crimper is the specialized tool used to attach wires to an RJ45 connector by compressing the connector onto the wires to create the proper electrical and mechanical connection. This is the standard tool for terminating twisted-pair Ethernet cables.

why.B: A cable stripper removes the outer jacket of cables but does not attach wires to connectors.
why.C: A punchdown tool is used to insert wires into punchdown blocks or keystone jacks, not to crimp RJ45 connectors.
why.D: A loopback plug is a testing device used to verify network port functionality, not a tool for creating connections.

prompt: A technician is working on a RAID 1 array that is apparently degraded. The technician verifies the RAM and power are both operating as expected.
Which of the following can the technician do to further isolate the issue?
explanation: Performing individual drive diagnostics is the appropriate next step to isolate which specific drive in the RAID 1 array is failing. Since RAM and power are confirmed working, testing each drive will identify the degraded component without making assumptions or taking corrective action prematurely.

why.B: Running chkdsk /f attempts to repair the file system but does not diagnose the underlying hardware issue causing the degradation.
why.C: Rebuilding the array should not be done until the technician identifies which drive has failed; rebuilding prematurely could cause data loss.
why.D: Reconfiguring as RAID 0 removes all redundancy and would result in data loss if any drive fails.

prompt: A company wants its RAID array set up so that it could lose multiple drives and still have redundancy.
Which of the following configurations should the company choose?
explanation: RAID 6 provides dual parity, allowing the array to tolerate the failure of two drives simultaneously while maintaining data availability and redundancy. This is the only configuration listed that can sustain multiple drive failures and still preserve all data.

why.A: RAID 0 provides no redundancy and any single drive failure results in complete data loss.
why.B: RAID 1 mirroring can only tolerate a single drive failure before losing redundancy.
why.C: RAID 5 with single parity can only tolerate one drive failure before redundancy is lost.

prompt: A user prints a spreadsheet in duplex mode. The spreadsheet is difficult to read because some of the columns spill onto the second side of the page.
Which of the following should the user do to prevent the issue but still print on both sides of the page?

options.text: Try a smaller font size in the spreadsheet.

explanation: Changing the page orientation from portrait to landscape expands the horizontal space available for columns, allowing the spreadsheet content to fit on one side of the page without spilling to the back. This maintains duplex printing while solving the readability issue.

why.A: Turning off duplex printing eliminates the desired double-sided printing functionality.
why.B: Reducing font size makes the spreadsheet harder to read, which contradicts the goal of improving readability.
why.D: Changing the print driver is unlikely to solve a layout problem related to page orientation and column width.

prompt: Which of the following cable types can be used to transfer data and video?
explanation: USB-C is a modern connector standard that supports both data transfer and video output
(via protocols like DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt 3), making it capable of transmitting both data and video signals simultaneously over a single cable.

why.B: HDMI transfers video and audio but not general data.
why.C: DisplayPort transfers video and audio but not general data.
why.D: VGA is an analog video-only standard that does not support data transfer.

prompt: Which of the following types of RAM is best suited to handle errors within the module itself?
explanation: Error-Correcting Code (ECC) RAM is specifically designed to detect and correct single-bit errors within the module itself, making it ideal for systems requiring high reliability such as servers and workstations where data integrity is critical.

why.A: DIMM is a physical form factor descriptor for RAM modules but does not indicate error correction capability.
why.B: Dual channel refers to the memory architecture configuration for bandwidth, not error correction.
why.D: SODIMM is a small form factor RAM module type used in laptops but lacks error correction capabilities.

prompt: A technician needs to move a workstation to a different logical network segment.
Which of the following technologies should the technician use?
explanation: A VLAN (Virtual Local Area Network) allows a technician to logically segment a workstation to a different network segment without requiring physical relocation of cables or network infrastructure, making it the appropriate technology for moving a workstation to a different logical network.

why.A: DHCP is used for automatic IP address assignment but does not control logical network segmentation.
why.C: DNS resolves domain names to IP addresses but does not segment workstations into different logical networks.
why.D: VPN creates secure remote connections but is not used to assign a local workstation to a different logical network segment.

prompt: After a technician installs a new motherboard, the computer will not start and fails POST. The technician verifies the power supply is functioning as expected, and the CPU is installed correctly.
Which of the following steps should the technician complete next?
explanation: After verifying the power supply and CPU installation, RAM is the next most common cause of POST failures on a new motherboard installation. RAM modules can appear properly seated but have poor contact, and reseating them often resolves no-boot issues. This is a quick, non-destructive troubleshooting step that should be attempted before more invasive measures like BIOS flashing or motherboard replacement.

why.A: BIOS flashing should only be attempted after basic hardware troubleshooting and is not a first-line response to POST failures.
why.B: While CMOS battery issues can cause problems, they typically result in incorrect system time or boot settings rather than complete POST failures on new installations.
why.D: Reinstalling the old motherboard is a last resort only after confirming the new motherboard is defective, not an early troubleshooting step.

prompt: Which of the following is an advantage of using VDI?

options.text: Authentication is not required on a domain.
Less manual configuration is needed for each workstation.
A virus is automatically contained locally.

answerText: Less manual configuration is needed for each
explanation: workstation.

Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) centralizes desktop management on servers, allowing administrators to deploy and configure desktop images once and push them to multiple users. This significantly reduces manual configuration needed for each individual workstation, as updates and settings are managed centrally. Users simply connect to their virtual desktop rather than having each physical machine individually configured.

why.A: VDI still requires authentication on a domain; in fact, domain authentication is typically more important in VDI environments for security.
why.B: VDI licensing can actually be more expensive due to server infrastructure and software licensing costs, not cheaper.
why.D: A virus on a virtual desktop is not automatically contained locally; it could potentially spread to the server or other virtual desktops if not properly isolated.

prompt: A user is unable to access secure applications on their tablet when working from home a couple days per week, but the applications work when in the office.
Which of the following services most likely needs to be reconfigured to allow for remote work?
explanation: Mobile Device Management (MDM) is the service responsible for enforcing security policies, certificates, and access controls on mobile devices. When a user cannot access secure applications remotely but can in the office, the MDM policy likely needs to be reconfigured to allow remote access or to properly provision security certificates and authentication for off-network connections. MDM controls which apps can run and
enforces security requirements for application access.

why.A: GPS is used for location services and has no relationship to accessing secure applications.
why.C: Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA) is a network security standard and would affect all network access equally, not just secure applications.
why.D: Near-field communication (NFC) is a short-range wireless technology and has no relevance to accessing secure enterprise applications.

prompt: A systems administrator deploys BitLocker to all devices. However, one of the desktop PCs is not able to encrypt the boot drive.
Which of the following should the administrator check?
explanation: BitLocker requires a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) chip to store encryption keys securely, especially for the boot drive. Without a functioning TPM 1.2 or higher, BitLocker cannot enable encryption on the boot drive. This is a hardware requirement that must be present and enabled in the system BIOS for BitLocker to function properly.

why.B: The CPU does not directly enable or disable BitLocker; it is not a prerequisite for BitLocker encryption.
why.C: RAM capacity or function does not affect BitLocker's ability to encrypt the boot drive.
why.D: The HDD type does not prevent BitLocker encryption; the issue is with security infrastructure, not storage hardware.

prompt: A technician is troubleshooting issues occurring on a user's mobile device. Applications and the OS have slow response times, even when performing simple tasks, such as writing an email. Additionally, new applications occasionally fail to launch.
Which of the following should the technician do next?

options.text: Move the device to a room with a colder temperature.
Check the battery health of the device.

explanation: Slow response times and applications failing to launch on a mobile device typically indicate insufficient available memory or processing resources. Closing unnecessary programs immediately frees up RAM and processing power, addressing the symptom directly. This is the logical first troubleshooting step before considering hardware replacement or factory reset, and it is non-destructive and quick to implement.

why.A: Temperature is unlikely to be the cause of slow response times and application failures unless the device is overheating, which would typically show thermal warnings.
why.C: Factory reset should only be done after other troubleshooting steps and will result in data loss; it is not the next logical step.
why.D: Battery health affects runtime and may cause unexpected shutdowns, but it does not directly cause slow performance or application launch failures.

prompt: A user connects their laptop to a projector in a conference room. Once connected, the user reports the screen is smaller at the bottom than at the top. The user tries restarting the laptop and then disconnecting and reconnecting the cable to the projector.
Which of the following should a technician do to resolve the issue?
explanation: When a projector image appears smaller at the bottom than at the top (or vice versa), this is a keystone distortion issue caused by the projector not being perpendicular to the projection surface. The keystone adjustment feature in projectors corrects this geometric distortion. Since basic troubleshooting (restart and cable reconnection) was already attempted, adjusting the keystone setting will correct the trapezoidal image.

why.A: Replacing the HDMI cable would not cause geometric distortion; this would affect signal quality, not image shape.
why.B: Power cycling the projector was essentially already done through the restart process and would not fix a keystone problem.
why.D: Increasing resolution does not correct keystone distortion; resolution affects image clarity, not geometric shape correction.

prompt: A projector has been shutting down after 30 minutes of use, and it has a strange smell. The technician confirms the power source is not the cause of the issue.
Which of the following steps should the technician take next to resolve this issue?
explanation: A projector shutting down after 30 minutes of use combined with a strange smell indicates a thermal shutdown due to overheating. A clogged or dirty filter prevents proper airflow and cooling, causing the projector to overheat and trigger automatic shutdown. The strange smell is likely from dust burning on hot components. Cleaning the filter restores proper ventilation and should resolve both the shutdown and odor issues.

why.A: A failed bulb would cause loss of light output or no image, not thermal shutdown with a burning smell.
why.B: Projector configuration settings do not cause thermal shutdown; this is a hardware heat dissipation issue.
why.D: Gamma settings affect image brightness and contrast, not thermal behavior or automatic shutdown.

prompt: A user reports that the printouts from a laser printer have lines and smudges on them. The printer is also intermittently misfeeding the paper.
Which of the following components should a technician replace to address this issue?
explanation: Lines and smudges on printouts combined with paper misfeeding indicate wear on the printer's mechanical components. The maintenance kit includes rubber rollers, separation pads, and other components that wear out during normal operation. These components directly affect paper feeding and toner transfer to paper. Replacing the maintenance kit addresses both the image quality issues (lines/smudges from worn rollers) and the paper misfeeding problem.

why.A: The fuser bonds toner to paper; a failing fuser would cause smudging but not the combination of lines and misfeeding typical of worn mechanical parts.
why.C: The corona wire affects toner charging; a faulty corona wire causes uneven toning but not the mechanical paper misfeeding described.
why.D: A toner cartridge issue would affect toner supply and image darkness, not the combination of lines, smudges, and paper misfeeding from mechanical wear.

prompt: A company has a main office and 20 branch offices. The company wants to have a backup network connection to allow connectivity if the main fiber connection goes down. The company does not want to create new infrastructure.
Which of the following should the company use?
explanation: Cellular provides a backup network connection without requiring new infrastructure installation. The company has existing cellular infrastructure available, and cellular networks can serve as a redundant WAN link when the primary fiber connection fails. Cable, DSL, and SAN either require new infrastructure, are unreliable for critical backups, or are not network connectivity solutions respectively.

why.A: Cable would require installing new cable infrastructure, which the company explicitly wants to avoid.
why.C: DSL would require new infrastructure and is slower and less reliable than cellular for backup purposes.
why.D: SAN is a storage area network, not a WAN backup connectivity solution.

prompt: Which of the following drive interfaces is typically used in server systems but not in home computers?
explanation: SAS (Serial Attached SCSI) is the standard drive interface in server systems but is rarely found in home computers. SAS provides superior reliability, hot-swap capability, and performance characteristics required for enterprise environments. While NVMe and PCIe are increasingly used in servers, they are now common in home computers. SATA is ubiquitous in both home and server systems.

why.A: NVMe is now commonly used in modern home computers and gaming systems.
why.C: SATA is the standard interface in both home computers and many server systems.
why.D: PCIe is increasingly common in consumer-grade computers for NVMe SSDs.

prompt: Which of the following could a user employ to maximize module bandwidth when selecting memory for a high-end gaming computer?
explanation: Channel configuration directly impacts module bandwidth by allowing dual-channel or quad-channel operation, which significantly increases the memory bandwidth available to the system. Running memory in multi-channel mode effectively doubles or quadruples bandwidth compared to single-channel operation. Error correction, RAM voltage, and physical module size do not directly maximize bandwidth.

why.A: Error correction improves reliability but does not maximize bandwidth.
why.B: RAM voltage affects stability and power consumption, not bandwidth capacity.
why.D: Physical module size affects capacity but not the bandwidth between modules and CPU.

prompt: A customer recently experienced a power outage at a SOHO. The customer does not think the components are connected properly. A print job continued running for several minutes after the power failed, but the customer was not able to interact with the computer.
Once the UPS stopped beeping, all functioning devices also turned off.
In case of a future power failure, the customer wants to have the most time available to save cloud documents and shut down the computer without losing any data.
INSTRUCTIONS
Based on the customer's requirements, connect the customer's devices to the proper outlets. Then, use the drop-down menus to select the power source for the surge protector and UPS.
This may require reselecting dropdowns or removing devices from their initial location.
Click on the + to add a device, and click the X to remove a device. Each device may only be used once.
summary: Connect devices to appropriate power outlets and configure surge protector and UPS power sources to maximize uptime during power failures.

pairs.match: Monitor, Wi-Fi router, Cable modem, and Computer

steps: 1. Both the surge protector and UPS must be powered from the wall outlet to receive initial power.
2. The computer and critical network devices (monitor, Wi-Fi router, cable modem) connect to the UPS to maintain power during outages.
3. The printer and scanner, which do not require uninterrupted operation, connect to the surge protector for protection only.
4. This configuration ensures the computer and network remain powered long enough for the user to save documents and shut down gracefully when the UPS battery runs low.

The customer experienced a situation where the printer continued running after power loss but the computer could not be used—indicating the printer was on UPS backup while the computer was not. The correct solution connects the computer, monitor, Wi-Fi router, and

cable modem to the UPS so they remain powered during an outage, giving the customer time to save cloud documents and perform an orderly shutdown. The printer and scanner attach to the surge protector since they do not require backup power. Both the surge protector and UPS draw power from the wall outlet, allowing them to recharge and protect devices during normal operation and to provide battery backup during failures.

prompt: A user reports poor performance on the application server.
INSTRUCTIONS
Click on Server 1 and Server 2 and review the information presented in each chart to determine which drives need to be replaced.
Select the appropriate replacement drive that should be used, for the least performance degradation to the server.
summary: Identify the failing/failed disk in each server and pick the correct replacement drive from that bay's dropdown.
steps: 1. Server 1's RAID-5 array shows Ready, but the physical disk chart flags Physical disk 1:2 with 'Failure predicted: Yes', so the drive in bay 2 must be swapped out before it fails.
2. Server 2's array is Degraded because Physical disk 1:5 is Offline and Failed, so the drive in bay 5 is the one to replace.
3. A RAID-5 member must match the existing members in size and interface, so Server 1's bay 2 gets a 4TB SAS 15k rpm disk, identical to the other 4TB SAS 15k rpm drives
in that array.

4. Server 2's remaining members are 2TB 7200rpm disks, so the replacement must be 2TB; the solution selects the 2TB SATA SSD, which matches capacity while giving the least performance degradation during and after the rebuild.

Two drives are at fault. In Server 1 the array is still healthy, but the disk chart predicts failure on Physical disk 1:2, so that drive is replaced proactively; because the array is built from 4TB SAS 15k rpm members, the replacement must be the identical 4TB SAS 15k rpm option, since a smaller or slower disk would shrink or slow the whole RAID-5 set. In Server 2 the array is already Degraded because Physical disk 1:5 is Offline and Failed, so bay 5 needs a new disk of at least the same 2TB capacity; the answer chosen is the 2TB SATA SSD, which keeps the capacity the array expects while being the fastest of the 2TB options offered, giving the smallest performance hit while the array rebuilds and afterwards.

prompt: An IT specialist compares Bluetooth and NFC technologies for mobile device connectivity.
Which of the following statements accurately describes a key difference between the two?

options.text: NFC is faster than Bluetooth when transferring large files between devices.
NFC consumes more power than Bluetooth, making it less suitable for devices in which battery conservation is crucial.
NFC requires pairing with the receiving host, whereas Bluetooth just needs the available connection.
NFC works best within a few centimeters, but Bluetooth can connect devices that are up to 32ft (10m) apart.

answerText: NFC works best within a few centimeters, but
explanation: Bluetooth can connect devices that are up to 32ft (10m) apart.

NFC operates best within a few centimeters (typically 4-10cm) for secure close-proximity communication, while Bluetooth can connect devices up to 32 feet (approximately 10 meters) apart. This is a fundamental difference reflecting their design purposes: NFC for secure short-range transactions and Bluetooth for general wireless connectivity over longer distances.

why.A: Bluetooth is faster than NFC for large file transfers; NFC is designed for small data exchanges.
why.B: NFC actually consumes less power than Bluetooth, making it ideal for battery-constrained devices.
why.C: NFC typically does not require pairing and works without prior connection setup, while Bluetooth requires pairing.

prompt: A help desk technician needs to work on a high-volume printer. Users have reported occasional paper jams and smudges appearing on printed documents.
Which of the following steps should the technician do next to address these issues?

options.text: Change all the ink or toner cartridges.

explanation: Paper jams and smudges on printed documents are classic symptoms of dirty rollers that transport paper through the printer. Cleaning the rollers is the first logical diagnostic step before more invasive solutions. This addresses both symptoms: rollers caked with paper dust cause jams, and dirty rollers deposit smudges on paper surfaces.

why.A: A full factory reset is excessive and unnecessary for mechanical issues related to paper feed.
why.C: Changing cartridges addresses toner/ink issues but not paper jams or smudging from mechanical problems.
why.D: Replacing the fuser is a major repair typically done only after other components are ruled out, not a first step.

prompt: A user reports that a phone’s integration features consistently stop and restart when charging the phone in a car. A technician checks the phone and finds no malicious applications.
Which of the following should the technician do to fix the issue?

options.text: Replace the cable with a longer cable.
Reinstall MDM software on the phone.

explanation: Integration features crashing and restarting when charging suggests a connectivity issue at the charging port. A dirty or corroded charging port causes intermittent electrical contact, triggering crashes when the device attempts to communicate with car integration systems. Cleaning the port restores proper electrical contact and resolves the issue.

why.B: Cable length is unrelated to software crashes; a longer cable would not fix an electrical contact problem.
