why.C: MDM software reinstallation is unnecessary when the issue is directly tied to charging events and port connectivity.
why.D: Battery discharge is unrelated to integration feature crashes and would not address the root electrical contact problem.

prompt: A technician sets up a conference room projector that begins to intermittently flicker. The projector is connected to a laptop via an HDMI cable.
When the technician connects the laptop to a monitor using the same cable, the issue persists.
Which of the following steps should the technician take to troubleshoot the display issue?

options.text: Adjust the resolution settings on the laptop.
Swap the HDMI cable with a new one.
Check and configure the refresh rate settings.

answerText: Swap the HDMI cable with a new one.
explanation: The flickering persists across two different display devices (projector and monitor) with the same HDMI cable, indicating the cable is the problem, not the displays or laptop. A faulty HDMI cable causing intermittent signal loss produces exactly this symptom. Swapping the cable is the most direct troubleshooting step to isolate and resolve the issue.

why.A: Resolution settings would not cause intermittent flickering, and the issue persists on different devices.
why.C: Replacing the projector is premature when the issue occurs on multiple displays with the same cable.
why.D: Refresh rate configuration might cause display issues but would not explain why the problem appears on both projector and monitor.

prompt: A SOHO customer runs an OS on a bare-metal server that has been EOL for almost a decade and is showing signs of failure. The application meets all the customer’s needs, and they want to continue using it. However, the developer went out of business, and there is no way to upgrade it.
A technician does not think the OS will run on modern hardware.
Which of the following will allow the customer to use the application long-term?

options.text: Continue to use the current system until failure.
Virtualize the entire system under a compatible hypervisor.
Containerize the application in a multitenant cloud environment.
Clone the disks and run the application from a USB enclosure.

answerText: Virtualize the entire system under a compatible
explanation: hypervisor.

Virtualizing the entire system under a compatible hypervisor allows the outdated OS and application to run on modern hardware without modification. The hypervisor abstracts the hardware layer, enabling the legacy OS to function as if it were on original hardware while running on current infrastructure. This provides long-term stability, easier backup/recovery, and maintenance capabilities.

why.A: Continuing with the failing hardware guarantees eventual failure and data loss.
why.C: Containerization requires application modifications and modern OS compatibility, which is not possible here.
why.D: Running from USB enclosure does not address the failing hardware and provides no long-term sustainability.

prompt: Which of the following network services is used to assign an IP address to a network host?
explanation: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) is specifically designed to automatically assign IP addresses to network hosts. DNS resolves domain names to IP addresses,
LDAP is a directory service, and SMTP handles email transmission—none of these assign IP addresses.

why.B: DNS resolves hostnames to IP addresses but does not assign them.
why.C: LDAP is a directory service protocol used for authentication and directory lookups.
why.D: SMTP is an email transmission protocol and has no role in IP address assignment.

prompt: Which of the following ports is commonly used for remote desktop connections?
explanation: Port 3389 is the standard port for Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP), which enables remote desktop connections. Port 137 is used for NetBIOS, port 445 for SMB/CIFS file sharing, and port 4443 is sometimes used for HTTPS or other secure services, but none are standard for remote desktop.

why.A: Port 137 is associated with NetBIOS name resolution, not remote desktop.
why.B: Port 445 is used for SMB/CIFS file sharing and network communications.
why.D: Port 4443 is sometimes used as an alternate HTTPS port but not for standard remote desktop.

prompt: Images and text from a laser printer smudge if touched.
Which of the following should a technician do to resolve the issue?
explanation: Smudging and transfer of images and text that can be wiped off indicates a fuser problem.

The fuser is the heated component that permanently bonds toner to paper; when it malfunctions, toner does not adhere properly and smudges easily. Low toner would result in faint printing, a maintenance kit addresses wear components, and dirty pickup rollers cause paper feed issues.

why.A: Low toner levels produce faint prints, not smudging that comes off when touched.
why.B: A maintenance kit addresses general wear but is not the primary cause of smudging.
why.D: Dirty pickup rollers cause paper feeding problems, not smudging of already-printed content.

prompt: A user reports their company-provided smartphone does not have internet access when the user is in the parking lot.
Which of the following should a technician check first?
explanation: When a smartphone has no internet in a specific location but the device itself is functional, the first check should be whether cellular data (3G/4G/5G/LTE) is enabled and configured. A SIM connection issue would typically prevent connectivity everywhere, hotspot capability is for sharing, and GPS is unrelated to internet access.

why.B: A faulty SIM connection would prevent connectivity in all locations, not just the parking lot.
why.C: Hotspot capability is for sharing internet with other devices, not for the phone's own connectivity.
why.D: GPS configuration does not affect cellular or mobile data connectivity.

prompt: Every day for a week, when a user turns on their computer, the time is wrong. A technician corrects the time, but the issue happens again.
Which of the following is most likely the cause of the issue?
explanation: The CMOS battery maintains the system time when the computer is powered off. A failing CMOS battery loses its charge and cannot retain the time, causing the system clock to reset each time the device powers on. NTP settings affect network time synchronization but wouldn't cause this recurring daily issue, and time zone settings would not reset each day.

why.A: A failing NIC would affect network connectivity, not the system clock.
why.B: Misconfigured NTP would cause continuous time drift if enabled, not daily resets at startup.
why.C: An incorrect time zone would display the wrong time consistently but not reset daily to an earlier time.

prompt: A company decides to subscribe to a cloud service to provide email for its employees.
Which of the following cloud models is the company adopting?
explanation: Email provided as a cloud service is Software-as-a-Service (SaaS), where the vendor manages the application, infrastructure, and data. The company simply uses the email service without managing underlying infrastructure. PaaS provides a development platform, IaaS provides virtual infrastructure, and DaaS provides virtual desktops.

why.A: PaaS provides a platform for developing applications, not a ready-to-use email service.
why.C: DaaS (Desktop-as-a-Service) provides virtual desktop environments, not email services.
why.D: IaaS provides virtual computing infrastructure but not managed business applications like email.

prompt: A customer built a computer for gaming, sourcing individual components and then assembling the system. The OS starts up, but within a few minutes the machine locks up. The customer brought the computer to a technician to diagnose the issue.
INSTRUCTIONS
Click on the BIOS system information and each component to view the specifications.
Select the appropriate cause and resolution for the issue.
summary: Select the cause of system lockup and the appropriate resolution from the dropdown menus.
steps: 1. The BIOS shows a CPU temperature of 100°C, which is critically high and indicates severe thermal stress.
2. The CPU is running at 4.5 GHz with a 10-core configuration, suggesting aggressive overclocking has been applied.
3. System lockup after a few minutes of operation is a classic symptom of thermal throttling or shutdown triggered by excessive heat.
4. Overclocking increases voltage and frequency, generating more heat than the liquid cooling system can dissipate.
5. Reducing CPU clock speed directly lowers heat generation and allows the cooling system to maintain safe temperatures.

The customer's gaming build exhibits critical thermal issues. The BIOS displays a CPU temperature of 100°C, which exceeds safe operating limits and triggers thermal protection mechanisms causing the system to lock up. The CPU is configured at 4.5 GHz, indicating overclocking has been applied. When a custom-built system with aggressive overclocking locks up after a few minutes, the root cause is typically overclocking-induced heat generation that overwhelms the cooling capacity. Although the system has liquid cooling, the aggressive clock speed produces more heat than the cooling solution can handle. The appropriate resolution is to lower the CPU clock speed, which reduces power consumption and heat output, allowing the liquid cooling system to maintain the CPU within a safe operating temperature range and preventing thermal shutdown.

prompt: A customer reports that a workstation has no internet connectivity. A technician confirms the port is disabled.
Which of the following is most likely responsible for the issue?
explanation: A managed switch is responsible for enabling or disabling network ports. If a technician confirms a port is disabled, the managed switch is most likely the cause, as administrators can selectively disable ports at the switch level. A patch panel is passive, a NIC failure would be a hardware issue, and a firewall typically blocks traffic rather than disabling physical ports.

why.A: A patch panel is a passive component that simply connects cables; it cannot disable ports.
why.B: A physical NIC failure would cause hardware issues but would not result in a disabled port setting.
why.D: A firewall blocks traffic but does not disable the physical network port itself.

prompt: A company is testing the latest model of a laptop. After turning on the laptop, there is a noticeable burning smell.
Which of the following steps should a technician take to troubleshoot the laptop issue? (Choose two.)

options.text: Turn it off and disconnect all power sources
Submit an emergency request to the local facilities manager
Check for foreign objects, liquid spills, and internal damage.
Contact the vendor and submit a return request.
Remove the device from the MDM

answerText: Turn it off and disconnect all power sources; Check for foreign objects, liquid spills, and internal damage.
explanation: When a device emits a burning smell, the immediate priority is safety: turn it off and disconnect all power to prevent fire or electrical hazard (A). Then, inspect for visible damage like foreign objects, liquid spills, or burned components to identify the root cause (C). Submitting a return request or facilities manager call is premature without diagnosis, trying alternate adapters could cause more damage, and MDM removal is irrelevant to the immediate hardware safety issue.

why.B: Facilities manager involvement is not appropriate for a device-level electrical safety issue.
why.D: Contacting vendor support is appropriate eventually, but first-aid diagnostics and safety checks come first.
why.E: MDM removal is an administrative action unrelated to troubleshooting a hardware malfunction.
why.F: Attempting an alternate adapter could cause additional damage if there is an electrical fault in the device.

prompt: A technician needs to figure out why a laser printer is intermittently not feeding paper to print. The technician verifies the issue by running several copy-and-print tests.
Which of the following should the technician do next?
explanation: When a laser printer intermittently fails to feed paper after confirming the issue through testing, the most likely cause is mechanical failure of the pickup rollers due to dust, debris, or wear. Cleaning the pickup rollers is the appropriate next troubleshooting step before considering component replacement. This addresses the physical mechanism responsible for paper feeding.

why.A: Driver updates address software issues, not mechanical paper feeding problems.
why.B: Paper size selection would cause consistent failures or error messages, not intermittent feeding issues.
why.D: The toner cartridge does not affect paper feeding functionality.

prompt: Which of the following can be used to logically segment networks?
explanation: A VLAN (Virtual Local Area Network) is specifically designed to logically segment networks by allowing multiple broadcast domains to exist on a single physical switch. VLANs enable logical separation of network traffic based on configuration rather than physical cabling, making them the correct tool for logical network segmentation.

why.A: MAC addresses identify physical devices but do not segment networks logically.
why.C: A NIC (Network Interface Card) is a physical hardware component, not a segmentation method.
why.D: DSL is a type of internet connection technology and has no role in network segmentation.

prompt: After troubleshooting a computer's connectivity, the network team determines there is a port-flapping issue. After plugging the patch cable into a different port, the issue persists.
Which of the following troubleshooting steps should a technician take next to resolve the issue?

options.text: Convert the patch cable to a crossover cable
Test the patch cable from the computer to the network closet
Verify the length of the patch cable meets current standards
Replace the patch cable from the device to the wall

answerText: Test the patch cable from the computer to the
explanation: network closet

Port flapping that persists across different switch ports indicates the problem is not with the switch port itself. The next logical step is to test the patch cable from the computer to the network closet to determine if the cable is defective, damaged, or out of specification. This isolates whether the issue is the cable itself rather than the infrastructure.

why.A: Crossover cables are for specific legacy scenarios and are not standard for modern network troubleshooting; auto-sensing eliminates this need.
why.C: Cable length should be verified, but testing the cable directly is the more immediate troubleshooting step to identify if it is faulty.
why.D: While the cable may ultimately need replacement, testing it first confirms whether replacement is actually necessary.

prompt: Which of the following statements best summarize managed vs unmanaged switches?

options.text: Unmanaged switches are generally more expensive.
Unmanaged switches have more security capabilities
Unmanaged switches start working as soon as they are plugged in to the network.

explanation: C. Unmanaged switches start working as soon as they are plugged in to the network.
D. Managed switches have more features

Unmanaged switches are plug-and-play devices that require no configuration and function immediately when powered on, making option C correct. Managed switches offer advanced features such as VLAN support, port mirroring, QoS, and security controls that unmanaged switches lack, making option D correct. Managed switches are typically more expensive and require configuration, contradicting options A, B, and E. Option F is incorrect as managed switches often consume more power due to additional processing.

why.A: Unmanaged switches are generally less expensive than managed switches.
why.B: Unmanaged switches have minimal to no security capabilities; managed switches provide security features.
why.E: Managed switches require configuration to function optimally, not zero configuration.
why.F: Managed switches typically consume more power due to processing overhead, not less.

prompt: A user is testing a new OS that is contained on a USB drive. The user wants the new OS to load automatically when the computer is turned on.
Which of the following should the user configure?
explanation: To make a USB drive automatically boot when the computer starts, the user must configure the boot options (boot order/boot sequence) in the BIOS/UEFI settings. This tells the system to prioritize the USB device in the boot sequence so the OS on the USB loads first during startup.

why.A: BIOS password protects access to BIOS settings but does not control which device boots.
why.B: Trusted Platform Module provides security and encryption features, not boot sequence control.
why.C: USB permissions relate to file system access and do not affect boot order configuration.

prompt: A technician is setting up a locally hosted environment for internal developers who need concurrent access to a wide array of test OSs.
Which of the following would best fulfill this requirement?
explanation: A hypervisor is the ideal solution for developers needing concurrent access to multiple test operating systems in a local environment. Hypervisors allow multiple virtual machines to run simultaneously on a single host, each with different operating systems, providing isolation and flexibility for testing without requiring physical hardware for each OS.

why.B: SaaS platforms are cloud-based and not locally hosted, contrary to the requirement.
why.C: A multiboot server can only run one OS at a time, not provide concurrent access to multiple test OSs.
why.D: A sandbox provides an isolated environment for testing but is not designed for managing multiple concurrent OS instances for developers.

prompt: An employee’s screen keeps flashing. Sometimes the picture goes out and comes back. The employee checks the power cord and confirms the device is plugged in fully.
Which of the following should a technician check for first?
explanation: Intermittent screen flashing with periodic signal loss is a classic symptom of a loose video

cable connection. Since the power cord has been verified, checking the video cable connection to both the monitor and graphics card (or motherboard) is the quickest and most common fix for this type of intermittent display issue.

why.B: A failing graphics card typically produces consistent artifacts or complete failure, not intermittent flashing.
why.C: Conflicting drivers would cause performance issues or crashes rather than periodic signal loss from the display.
why.D: A swollen capacitor is a hardware defect that would cause system instability or failure, not specifically intermittent display flashing.

prompt: A technician is setting up a scan-to-SMB function on a multifunction printer.
Which of the following connection types should the technician configure?
explanation: SMB (Server Message Block) is a network file sharing protocol used to access shared folders and files on a network. For scan-to-SMB functionality, the technician must configure the printer to connect to a network share (a shared folder on a server or computer) where scanned documents will be stored.

why.A: Email server configuration is used for scan-to-email functionality, not scan-to-SMB.
why.B: SFTP is a secure file transfer protocol primarily for remote access and file transfer, not for accessing local network shares via SMB.
why.D: Print services relate to the printing function of the multifunction device, not document scanning and storage.

prompt: A user reports that the print quality of their desk printer is poor. A technician replaces the ink cartridge, but this does not resolve the issue.
Which of the following should the technician do next?
explanation: When print quality remains poor after replacing ink cartridges, the issue is typically hardware-related rather than consumable-related. Dirty printheads are a common cause of poor print quality, streaking, or faded output. Cleaning the printheads is the logical next troubleshooting step before considering more invasive repairs or replacement parts.

why.A: Pickup rollers affect paper feed issues, not print quality.
why.C: Paper type affects output appearance but wouldn't cause poor quality across all papers if the cartridge replacement didn't help.
why.D: Ribbon is not used in modern inkjet printers and is irrelevant to this scenario.

prompt: An end user reports that their laptop shuts down when they undock it. Even when using a new charging cable, the issue persists.
Which of the following should the technician do next?
explanation: A laptop shutting down upon undocking despite using a new charging cable points to a battery issue. The system likely requires minimum power from the battery to remain stable during the docking transition. A faulty battery cannot hold charge and triggers a critical power event, causing shutdown. Since a new cable didn't resolve it, the battery itself is the failing component.

why.A: BIOS flashing is not a standard troubleshooting step for power-related issues and could cause data loss.
why.B: Driver updates may help with power management but wouldn't address a failing battery.
why.C: A different charger has functionally been tested with the new cable; the issue persists regardless of charging equipment.

prompt: A company provides cell phones to employees who travel internationally. An employee brings their phone to the help desk so the necessary equipment can be installed. However, the technician cannot install any new hardware on the phone.
Which of the following will the technician require so the phone can connect to a different provider?
explanation: eSIM (embedded SIM) is a software-based SIM that allows international travelers to connect to different providers without physical hardware installation. Since the technician cannot install physical hardware on the phone, eSIM is the solution that enables switching providers digitally without requiring any additional hardware components to be added to the device.

why.A: USB-C is a charging/data port and does not enable provider switching.
why.B: SD cards are storage expansion and do not relate to cellular provider connectivity.
why.D: MDM (Mobile Device Management) is a management platform and does not enable switching to different providers.

prompt: Which of the following internet connection types provides the fastest speeds and greatest coverage in less populated areas with minimal infrastructure?
explanation: Cellular networks provide the greatest coverage in less populated areas with minimal infrastructure because they rely on distributed cell towers rather than hardwired infrastructure. While cellular speeds may not always match fiber in urban areas, it offers the best combination of speed and coverage for remote and sparsely developed regions where fiber, cable, and DSL infrastructure is unavailable.

why.A: Fiber requires extensive underground or aerial infrastructure that is not economical in less populated areas.
why.B: Cable requires hardwired infrastructure (coaxial lines) that is not deployed in rural areas.
why.C: DSL requires proximity to telephone lines and is unavailable in many less populated regions.

prompt: Which of the following ports should a technician disable to increase the security of remote connectivity?
explanation: Port 23 is Telnet, an unencrypted remote access protocol that transmits credentials in plaintext. It is a major security vulnerability and should be disabled in favor of SSH (port 22), which provides encrypted remote connectivity. Disabling Telnet is a fundamental security hardening practice for any system requiring remote access.

why.A: Port 22 is SSH, the secure alternative to Telnet and should remain enabled for secure remote access.
why.C: Port 25 is SMTP (email) and is not a remote connectivity port.
why.D: Port 53 is DNS and is essential for name resolution across the network.

prompt: A network operations analyst receives an automated alert regarding a server with an array. The analyst walks over to the server and sees a blinking orange light at the hard disk bay. The server is configured for RAID 1. Which of the following should the analyst do to resolve this issue?

options.text: Undo the array and create a new one
Replace the hard disk and rebuild the array

answerText: Replace the hard disk and rebuild the array
explanation: A blinking orange light at a hard disk bay indicates a failed or failing drive. In RAID 1 (mirroring), one drive can fail while maintaining data integrity through the redundant copy. The correct procedure is to replace the failed disk and rebuild the array, which automatically resynchronizes data from the healthy drive to the new one.

why.A: Changing to RAID 0 (striping) eliminates redundancy and would result in data loss if a drive fails.
why.B: Undoing and recreating the array would cause data loss and is unnecessary when RAID handles rebuilds.
why.C: Firmware updates do not address a hardware failure indicated by the blinking light.

prompt: A user returns from a trip and discovers a computer that is connected to the LAN times out intermittently. Upon investigation, a technician finds the RJ45 pin is not properly terminated.
Which of the following networking tools is most appropriate to fix the issue?
explanation: A crimper is the tool used to properly terminate RJ45 connectors onto Ethernet cable. When a pin is not properly terminated, the connector must be removed and recrimped onto the cable using a crimper tool to establish proper contact and restore network connectivity.

why.A: A toner probe is used to trace and identify cables in a run, not to terminate connectors.
why.B: A cable tester diagnoses existing connections but cannot fix termination issues.
why.C: A punchdown tool is used for terminating cables on patch panels and wall jacks, not for RJ45 connectors on the end of cables.

prompt: A technician upgrades a PC with two DIMMs, for a total of 32GB. After installing the two DIMMs, the user notices the OS is reporting only 16GB.
Which of the following tasks should the technician perform to resolve the issue in the most rapid, cost-effective way possible?

options.text: Update the OS to the latest version

explanation: When newly installed RAM is not fully recognized by the OS, the most common and rapid fix is to reseat the DIMMs in different slots. RAM modules must be fully inserted into compatible slots, and sometimes they are not properly seated or installed in slots that do not support the full capacity. Reinstalling them ensures proper contact and correct slot assignment, which is the fastest and most cost-effective resolution.

why.A: Rolling back system updates is unlikely to enable recognition of hardware and wastes troubleshooting time.
why.C: OS updates do not cause unrecognized RAM and introduce unnecessary complexity.
why.D: Replacing the motherboard is expensive and premature when a simple reseat typically resolves the issue.

prompt: Which of the following internet connection types is the best for extremely high data transfer with symmetrical upload and download speeds?
explanation: Fiber optic connections provide the highest data transfer speeds with symmetrical upload and download capabilities, making it ideal for extremely high data transfer requirements. DSL is asymmetrical with slower speeds, cellular has limited bandwidth and latency issues, and satellite suffers from high latency and asymmetrical speeds.

why.A: DSL provides asymmetrical speeds with slower upload than download capabilities.
why.B: Cellular connections have limited bandwidth and are not suitable for extremely high data transfer.
why.D: Satellite connections have high latency and asymmetrical speeds, making them unsuitable for this requirement.

prompt: A company wants to have fast read speeds for its locally stored data.
Which of the following configurations has the lowest cost to fulfill this requirement?
explanation: RAID 0 (striping) provides the fastest read speeds by distributing data across multiple drives and requires only two drives minimum, making it the lowest cost option for high read speed requirements. RAID 1, 5, and 10 all include redundancy overhead that increases cost without improving read speed performance.

why.B: RAID 1 (mirroring) adds cost through redundancy without improving read speeds over RAID 0.
why.C: RAID 5 includes parity calculations and requires at least three drives, increasing cost compared to RAID 0.
why.D: RAID 10 combines mirroring and striping, requiring four drives minimum and significantly higher cost than RAID 0.

prompt: Which of the following connectors can be used to charge most modern mobile devices and may have the capacity to send data audio, and video?
explanation: USB-C is the modern universal standard connector supported by most current mobile devices and has full capabilities for charging, data transfer, audio, and video transmission. Lightning is proprietary to Apple devices only, while MicroUSB and MiniUSB are older standards with limited adoption on modern devices.

why.A: Lightning is proprietary to Apple devices and not universally used across most modern mobile devices.
why.C: MicroUSB is an older standard increasingly phased out on modern devices in favor of USB-C.
why.D: MiniUSB is an obsolete connector rarely found on modern mobile devices.

prompt: Which of the following devices has ACL capabilities?
explanation: A firewall has ACL (Access Control List) capabilities to filter traffic based on defined rules and policies. PoE injectors only supply power, DSL is a connection type without filtering capability, and unmanaged switches operate without any intelligence or ACL functionality.

why.A: A PoE injector is a power delivery device without filtering or ACL capabilities.
why.B: DSL is an internet connection type that does not provide ACL functionality.
why.D: An unmanaged switch has no intelligence or capability to implement access control lists.

prompt: A user would like to connect a laptop to a monitor, keyboard, and mouse when in the office. The user prefers to use as few cables as possible.
Which of the following would best achieve that goal?
explanation: A docking station connects to a laptop via a single cable and provides connections for monitor, keyboard, mouse, and other peripherals, requiring the fewest cables overall. Bluetooth and NFC are wireless but would still require separate connections for each device, and a managed switch provides network connectivity only.

why.A: Bluetooth would require pairing each device separately and does not connect a monitor.
why.B: A managed switch provides only network connectivity, not monitor, keyboard, or mouse connections.
why.D: Near-field communication has very limited range and bandwidth, unsuitable for peripheral connections.

prompt: A user keeps getting an error message when trying to print a letter. The printer is normally used to print cards and invitations. The user tries printing from a different computer, but the issue persists.
Which of the following should the user do to resolve the issue?
explanation: The printer is normally used for cards and invitations but is now printing a letter, suggesting the issue is a paper tray or format setting mismatch rather than a hardware problem. Changing the paper tray setting would resolve the error since the printer likely needs different settings for regular paper versus card stock. The error persists across multiple computers, ruling out a single computer issue.

why.A: Printing fewer pages would not resolve a settings mismatch issue.
why.B: The user wants to print a letter on regular paper, not card stock, so changing to card stock is incorrect.
why.C: The hardware (rollers) likely functions properly given the printer works for its normal purpose; the issue is a settings problem.

prompt: Which of the following should a company use to implement automatic time synchronization?
explanation: NTP (Network Time Protocol) is the standard protocol specifically designed for automatic time synchronization across network devices. DHCP assigns IP addresses, UTM provides unified threat management, and AAA handles authentication, authorization, and accounting—none of these are designed for time synchronization.

why.A: DHCP is for IP address assignment, not time synchronization.
why.B: UTM (Unified Threat Management) is a security solution, not a time synchronization tool.
why.D: AAA (Authentication, Authorization, Accounting) handles security and access control, not time synchronization.

prompt: An end user reports that their laptop has a blank screen. A technician observes the keyboard lights are on, and the fan is running.
Which of the following should the technician do next?
explanation: Since the keyboard lights are on and the fan is running, the laptop is powered and functional. The next logical diagnostic step is to connect an external monitor to determine if the issue is with the laptop's display hardware or the video output, which helps narrow down whether it's a display panel, inverter, or cable problem before attempting repairs.

why.A: While the ribbon cable could be an issue, external monitor testing should be performed first to isolate the problem.
why.B: Vendor support should be contacted only after basic troubleshooting is complete.
why.C: Replacing the inverter is a repair step that should only occur after confirming the display hardware is the problem.

prompt: Which of the following minimizes the time it takes to connect a display, keyboard, mouse, and network cable to a laptop?
explanation: A port replicator is specifically designed to connect multiple peripherals (display, keyboard, mouse, network) to a laptop through a single connection point, minimizing setup time. Lightning is an Apple connector with limited device support, USB hubs don't support all these devices simultaneously, and Bluetooth lacks the bandwidth and reliability for all these connections at once.

why.A: Lightning is an Apple-specific interface that doesn't support all four device types mentioned.
why.C: USB hubs primarily handle data peripherals and cannot efficiently connect displays or network cables.
why.D: Bluetooth is wireless only, cannot power devices, and lacks sufficient bandwidth for simultaneous multi-device connectivity.

prompt: A multifunction printer in a small office recently had issues with scan-to-email functionality. The manufacturer has an update ready to fix the printer issues.
Which of the following would a technician most likely deploy to remediate the issue?
explanation: Firmware updates are deployed to the printer's internal software to fix hardware-level functionality issues like scan-to-email capabilities. Drivers are for computer-printer communication, OS updates affect the computer not the printer, and HSM (Hardware Security Module) is unrelated to printer function.

why.B: Drivers control communication between a computer and printer but don't fix internal printer functionality issues.
why.C: OS updates affect the operating system, not the printer's internal scan-to-email functionality.
why.D: HSM (Hardware Security Module) is a security device unrelated to printer troubleshooting.

prompt: A technician is setting up a new SOHO wireless router. According to security best practices, which of the following should the technician do first?
explanation: Changing the default password should be done first as it immediately secures access to the router's administration interface, preventing unauthorized configuration changes. Encryption, static IP assignment, and factory reset are important but secondary to establishing secure admin access first.

why.A: While encryption is essential, it cannot be properly configured if the router is still accessible with default credentials.
why.B: Assigning a static IP is a network configuration task that should follow security hardening.
why.D: Resetting the router would undo any configuration already in place and is counterproductive during initial setup.

prompt: Which of the following can carry data and electricity to network devices? (Choose two.)
explanation: A PoE injector actively adds electrical power to network cables, and PoE itself refers to the standard that enables this dual data-and-power transmission over Ethernet cables. These are the only options that specifically carry both data and electricity to network devices as their primary function.

why.A: Routers receive power separately and do not carry electricity to other devices.
why.C: Cable modems receive power through separate connections and don't distribute power to devices.
why.D: Access points require separate power connections and do not provide power to connected devices.
why.F: Unmanaged switches pass through data only and do not provide power to devices.

prompt: A company deploys its infrastructure in self-operated data centers. The company recently migrated some of its applications to a public cloud.
Which of the following most accurately describes the cloud model the company is following?
explanation: A hybrid cloud model combines private infrastructure (self-operated data centers) with public cloud services. This company maintains on-premises data centers while also using public cloud resources, which is the defining characteristic of a hybrid deployment.

why.A: Public cloud means all infrastructure is hosted by a third party, not self-operated.
why.C: Community cloud serves a specific community of organizations with shared concerns, not a single company with mixed infrastructure.
why.D: Private cloud means all infrastructure is self-operated and dedicated to one organization, with no public cloud component.

prompt: A technician is setting up a new multifunction device to be used over a shared network connection. Copier functions need to be restricted to only office employees.
Which of the following should the technician perform after configuring the device to use a print server that exists on the domain?
explanation: User authentication restricts device functionality based on user identity and credentials, allowing only office employees to use copier functions. This enforces the access control requirement after the device is configured to use the domain print server.

why.A: SMTP implementation is for email transmission and doesn't restrict copier access to specific users.
why.B: Firmware updates modify device software but don't inherently restrict functionality based on user identity.
why.D: SMB configuration enables network file sharing but does not provide user-based access restrictions for device functions.

prompt: Which of the following networking devices is used to create a mesh network?
explanation: Access points are the primary networking devices used to create mesh networks, where multiple access points communicate with each other to extend coverage and provide
redundant connections. Modems and ONT handle internet connectivity, while DSL is a connection type, none of which create mesh configurations.

why.A: Modems convert ISP signals to usable data but do not create mesh network topologies.
why.B: DSL is a connectivity technology type, not a physical device that creates mesh networks.
why.D: ONT (Optical Network Terminal) terminates fiber connections but does not create mesh network configurations.

prompt: Which of the following display technologies typically provides the highest contrast?
explanation: OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) displays provide the highest contrast because each pixel produces its own light and can turn completely off independently, creating perfect blacks and infinite contrast ratios. IPS, TN, and VA panels use backlighting which cannot achieve true blacks.

why.A: IPS panels offer good color accuracy and wide viewing angles but use backlighting that prevents true blacks.
why.C: TN panels have fast response times but typically offer lower contrast than VA and cannot match OLED performance.
why.D: VA panels provide good contrast compared to IPS and TN but still cannot achieve the infinite contrast of OLED technology.

prompt: Which of the following types of RAM would most likely be used in a server?
explanation: ECC (Error-Correcting Code) RAM is the standard for servers because it detects and corrects single-bit memory errors, ensuring data integrity and system reliability. Servers require this protection due to their mission-critical nature and continuous operation, making ECC the most appropriate choice for server environments.

why.A: SODIMM is a small form factor RAM used in laptops and compact devices, not servers.
why.C: Unbuffered RAM lacks error correction and is typically found in consumer-grade systems, not servers.
why.D: DDR3 is a speed/generation designation that can apply to any RAM type; ECC DDR3 exists, but DDR3 alone does not indicate server-grade memory.

prompt: A company migrates a local application to an internal cloud platform.
Which of the following best describes this cloud platform?
explanation: An internal cloud platform that is migrated locally within a company's infrastructure is a private cloud. Private clouds are owned and operated by the organization itself, providing dedicated resources and control over the environment, as opposed to public clouds shared across multiple tenants.

why.B: Public cloud services are provided by third-party vendors and accessible to the general public, not internal-only.
why.C: Community clouds serve a specific group of organizations with shared interests, not a single company's internal migration.
why.D: Hybrid clouds combine both private and public cloud resources; an internal-only migration describes a pure private cloud.

prompt: A user purchases a new mobile phone and tries to connect it to the corporate communications and email applications without success.
Which of the following should a technician do to allow the phone to connect?

options.text: Enroll the device in the MDM software.
Complete the company's BYOD training process

answerText: Enroll the device in the MDM software.
explanation: Enrolling the device in MDM (Mobile Device Management) software is the standard procedure to allow corporate devices to access company communications and email applications. MDM establishes device compliance, security policies, and access controls necessary for corporate network connectivity.

why.A: Biometric security is a user authentication method but does not directly enable device enrollment or corporate application access.
why.B: LTE hotspot connectivity allows the phone to share internet but does not provide access to corporate applications without proper device enrollment.
why.D: BYOD training is a process for understanding policies but does not technically enable device connection to corporate systems.

prompt: Which of the following is the ability to automatically increase and decrease instances based on demand?
explanation: Elasticity is the ability to automatically increase and decrease computational resources (instances, storage, etc.) based on current demand. This on-demand scaling ensures efficient resource utilization and cost optimization in cloud environments.

why.A: Availability refers to system uptime and reliability, not automatic scaling based on demand.
why.B: Scalability is the capacity to grow, but does not necessarily imply automatic adjustment; elasticity specifically means automatic scaling.
why.C: Multitenancy is the ability of an application to serve multiple customers in a shared environment, unrelated to demand-based scaling.

prompt: A technician sets up secure print and configures an NFC device that will authenticate users for access.
Which of the following will the NFC device most likely use to authenticate?
explanation: NFC (Near Field Communication) devices most commonly use badging for authentication, where users present or tap an NFC badge or card to authenticate access to secure print systems. This contactless method is efficient and widely deployed in enterprise printing environments.

why.B: Passwords are knowledge-based factors typically entered via keyboards, not suited to NFC device authentication.
why.C: Passcodes are numeric PIN codes entered manually, not the typical authentication method for NFC devices at print systems.
why.D: While biometrics could theoretically be used, NFC devices specifically leverage badge/card-based identification rather than biometric scanning.

prompt: A customer recently lost data due to several unexpected shutdowns. Data integrity is important to the customer.
Which of the following features should the technician choose to prevent data loss?
explanation: An Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) provides backup battery power during unexpected shutdowns and power failures, allowing systems to continue operating and properly shut down without data loss. This is essential for data integrity when facing unexpected power events.

why.A: A redundant power supply provides failover within the device but does not protect against complete power loss or shutdowns.
why.C: A modular power supply is a design feature allowing component replacement but offers no protection against power failures.
why.D: A high-efficiency power supply reduces energy waste but does not prevent data loss during unexpected shutdowns.

prompt: Which of the following allows a physical server to host multiple virtual machines?
explanation: A hypervisor is the virtualization software that allows a physical server to host and manage multiple virtual machines simultaneously. It abstracts the hardware resources and allocates them to individual VMs, enabling efficient server consolidation.

why.A: Cross-platform virtualization refers to running VMs across different operating systems or platforms, not the core technology enabling multiple VMs on one physical server.
why.C: A sandbox is an isolated environment for testing/security purposes, not a mechanism for hosting multiple production virtual machines.
why.D: SaaS (Software as a Service) is a cloud service delivery model, not a virtualization technology for hosting VMs.

prompt: Which of the following virtualization technologies is best suited for running microservices?
explanation: Containers are the best virtualization technology for microservices because they provide lightweight, isolated application environments with minimal overhead. Containers enable fast deployment, easy scaling, and efficient resource usage—all critical for microservices architectures.

why.B: VDI (Virtual Desktop Infrastructure) is designed for virtualizing desktop environments, not for running microservices applications.
why.C: Type 2 hypervisors run on host operating systems and are heavier than containers, making them inefficient for microservices deployment.
why.D: Type 1 hypervisors are bare-metal solutions designed for full virtual machines, not optimized for the lightweight, rapid scaling needs of microservices.

prompt: An IT specialist sets up a new computer for a user who requires a high-end video card and the fastest hard drive possible.
Which of the following connectors should the specialist verify are available on the motherboard? (Choose two.)
explanation: For a high-end video card and fastest storage, the specialist needs to verify NVMe (M.2) slots for the fastest SSDs and PCIe slots (typically PCIe x16) for the high-end video card. NVMe drives connect via M.2 slots on the motherboard and offer the fastest storage performance. PCIe slots are essential for installing discrete graphics cards. Both are critical for this user's requirements.

why.A: Molex connectors are legacy power connectors; modern components use SATA power or direct motherboard connections.
why.C: SATA is slower than NVMe and is not the fastest hard drive option available.
why.D: FireWire is an outdated external connector not relevant to internal component installation.
why.E: USB-C is an external connector standard, not a motherboard slot for internal components like video cards or storage.

prompt: Which of the following tools is best to track where an Ethernet cable is patched?
explanation: A toner probe (or tone generator and probe kit) traces Ethernet cables through walls and patch panels by detecting the tone signal sent through the cable. It's the industry-standard tool for locating and tracking where a cable terminates or is patched in a network infrastructure.

why.A: A crimper is used to attach connectors to cable ends, not to track existing cables.
why.B: A punchdown tool is used to insert wires into keystone jacks or patch panels, not to trace cables.
why.C: A cable stripper removes insulation from cables for termination, not for tracking.

prompt: A user’s phone does not respond to touch. A technician inspects the phone but does not see any evidence of physical damage. The technician restarts the device, which does not fix the issue.
Which of the following components should the technician examine next?
explanation: The digitizer is the component responsible for detecting touch input on a smartphone screen. If touch is not responding and there's no visible physical damage, the digitizer has likely failed or become unresponsive. It's the logical next component to examine after ruling out simple fixes like restarting.

why.A: Battery issues would cause power problems, not specifically touch unresponsiveness.
why.B: The screen itself can display visually without the digitizer working; the screen layer and digitizer are separate components.
why.C: A stylus is an optional accessory, not a core component for touch functionality.

prompt: A user is having trouble with the location services on their smartphone. Location-based applications show incorrect positions when the user is traveling. This issue affects the user's ability to navigate and use location-dependent applications.
Which of the following is the best way to resolve this issue?
explanation: Enabling Wi-Fi to assist GPS (known as Assisted GPS or A-GPS) improves location accuracy and helps lock onto satellites faster, especially when signal is weak or obstructed. This is the most direct solution for incorrect GPS positioning during travel, as Wi-Fi access points provide additional location reference data.

why.A: Downloading a third-party mapping application doesn't fix the underlying GPS positioning issue.
why.B: Resetting network settings may disrupt connectivity rather than improve GPS accuracy.
why.D: Restarting alone won't resolve GPS accuracy problems; the device needs additional assistance from A-GPS.

prompt: A user can connect their laptop to the internet in the main office. However, when the user places the laptop on top of a motor on the factory floor, there is no internet connectivity.
Which of the following is the most likely cause of this issue?
explanation: A motor on the factory floor generates significant electromagnetic interference that disrupts wireless signals. The laptop connects fine in the main office but loses connectivity when placed near the motor, which is classic RF interference behavior. This is the most likely cause of the connectivity loss in that specific location.

why.A: Jitter affects packet timing variability, not complete loss of connectivity.
why.B: Insufficient power levels would affect signal strength gradually, not cause complete dropout based on physical location.
why.D: High latency causes delay but not complete loss of internet connectivity.

prompt: Which of the following is a characteristic of an NVMe drive?
explanation: NVMe drives use the M.2 interface form factor, which is a small, compact slot on modern motherboards. This is the defining physical characteristic of NVMe drives, enabling their fast performance through direct connection to the motherboard's PCIe bus.

why.B: NVMe drives are typically 2.5-inch or M.2 form factors, not 3.5-inch external.
why.C: RPM (revolutions per minute) applies to mechanical hard drives, not solid-state NVMe drives.
why.D: Molex connectors are legacy; NVMe drives connect directly to M.2 motherboard slots without separate power connectors.

prompt: Which of the following connector types is associated with coaxial terminations serving cable internet deployments?
explanation: The F-type connector is the standard coaxial termination used for cable television and cable internet deployments. It's a threaded connector specifically designed for RG-6 and similar coaxial cables used in broadband infrastructure.

why.A: DB9 is a serial connector used for RS-232 communication, not cable internet.
why.B: ST is a fiber optic connector, not a coaxial termination.
why.D: RJ45 is used for Ethernet twisted-pair, not coaxial cable internet terminations.

prompt: A technician receives several complaints from the same office about VoIP calls sounding broken up, being difficult to hear, and having lagging audio. The technician arrives on-site and runs an internet speed test on several wired and wireless computers. Internet speed seems normal throughout the office.
Which of the following should the technician do to fix the call issues?

options.text: Change the encryption from WPA3 to WPA2

explanation: Quality of Service (QoS) prioritizes VoIP traffic in the router, ensuring voice packets receive priority over other network traffic. Since internet speed is normal but VoIP calls are broken up with lagging audio, the issue is likely congestion or other traffic competing for
bandwidth. Enabling QoS will prioritize VoIP traffic and resolve the audio quality issues.

why.B: PoE (Power over Ethernet) provides power to devices; it doesn't address VoIP call quality issues.
why.C: Changing WPA3 to WPA2 would degrade security and has no bearing on VoIP audio quality.
why.D: MAC address filtering is a security measure that doesn't improve VoIP call quality.

prompt: A technician needs to update a web server’s IPv4 address in a DNS server.
Which of the following records should the technician update?
explanation: An A record maps a hostname to an IPv4 address. When a technician needs to update a web server's IPv4 address in DNS, they must update the A record. This is the fundamental DNS record type used for IPv4 address resolution.

why.A: AAAA records map hostnames to IPv6 addresses, not IPv4.
why.B: MX records specify mail exchange servers for email routing.
why.C: CNAME records create aliases for existing domain names, not IP mappings.

prompt: A technician needs to prepare a conference room for a meeting. The technician connects the laptop to the LCD projector and audio system, and then verifies the connectivity of each device. The meeting begins, but the visual presentation suddenly cuts off 30 minutes later. The audio continues to play without interruption. The technician brings in a backup laptop and connects it to the projector. The meeting continues without issue for 15 minutes until the presentation suddenly cuts off again.
Which of the following should the technician do to resolve this issue?
explanation: The pattern of the display cutting off after about 15-30 minutes of use on multiple laptops, while audio continues uninterrupted, strongly suggests thermal shutdown of the projector. A clogged or dirty filter causes the projector to overheat and shut down. Since this happens consistently across different laptops and the audio system works fine, the issue is specific to the projector itself, not the video connection or source devices.

why.A: Audio output on the laptop is not relevant since the audio system works fine.
why.B: Input source verification would not cause intermittent shutdowns; the device would either not display or display consistently.
why.C: Burn-in on the display would not cause the visual presentation to cut off suddenly; it would appear as image persistence.
why.D: Cable damage would typically cause immediate connection failure, not delayed shutdown after 15-30 minutes of operation.

prompt: A technician installs an upgraded wireless access point. The technician then notices the activity light comes on briefly and turns off. The access point continues to exhibit this behavior repeatedly and does not come online.
Which of the following is the most likely cause of this issue?
explanation: Port flapping occurs when a port rapidly cycles between up and down states, causing the activity light to blink on and off repeatedly. This pattern of the activity light coming on briefly and turning off repeatedly, combined with the access point not coming online, is characteristic of port flapping. This often results from hardware issues, loose connections, or incompatibilities with the connected switch port.

why.A: High latency would not cause the activity light to cycle on and off; the device would still come online.
why.C: External interference might cause connectivity issues but would not produce the specific symptom of repeated activity light cycling.
why.D: Channel conflict would affect wireless performance after the device comes online, not prevent it from coming online with cycling activity lights.

prompt: A technician is setting up a workstation.
Which of the following settings should the technician configure to ensure that users can connect to the network? (Choose three.)
explanation: To connect a workstation to a network, three fundamental settings must be configured: the IP address (the device's network identifier), the subnet mask (which determines the local network range), and the gateway (which provides the route to networks outside the local subnet). These three components form the minimum required static network configuration for connectivity.

why.A: APIPA is an automatic fallback mechanism, not a required configuration setting for connecting to a network.
why.E: Static routes are advanced routing configurations needed only for specific network topologies, not for basic workstation connectivity.
why.F: UPnP settings are optional features for device discovery and are not required for basic network connectivity.
why.G: NAT rules are firewall/router configurations, not workstation settings needed for network connection.
why.H: MAC filters are security controls on network devices, not settings required on the workstation itself for connectivity.

prompt: A major retailer is moving its online shopping website to the cloud and wants to expand its server resources as needed during busier shopping days.
Which of the following should the retailer consider?
explanation: Elasticity is the cloud characteristic that allows resources to automatically scale up or down based on demand. The retailer's need to expand server resources during busier shopping days and presumably contract them during slower periods is a direct definition of elasticity—the ability to dynamically provision and deprovision resources to match current workload requirements.

why.A: Location refers to data center geographic placement and is not related to dynamic resource expansion needs.
why.C: Availability refers to service uptime and reliability, not the ability to scale resources based on demand.
why.D: Multitenancy refers to multiple customers sharing infrastructure, which is not the primary concern for scaling resources based on shopping traffic patterns.

prompt: A network printer does not release a user's final print job from the queue, but the user's other print jobs successfully printed a few moments before. Other users can print without issues.
Which of the following should the user check first to solve the issue?

options.text: If the print job is configured to a tray or manual feed
If the computer and printer are connected to the same network
If the print queue is full and will not allow additional jobs
If the printer has stopped due to empty trays

answerText: If the print job is configured to a tray or manual feed
explanation: When a specific print job fails to release from the queue while other jobs printed

successfully, the issue is typically related to that particular job's configuration. A job configured to a specific tray or manual feed setting that is unavailable will remain stuck in the queue. This is the first troubleshooting step because it's job-specific and explains why other users and earlier jobs were successful.

why.B: Network connectivity is unlikely since other print jobs from the same user succeeded moments before, indicating the connection is functional.
why.C: A full print queue would prevent new jobs from being accepted, but this user's other jobs already printed, so the queue is functioning.
why.D: Empty trays would prevent all jobs from printing or would have stopped the previous jobs; earlier jobs from this user printed successfully.

prompt: A technician is troubleshooting a workstation that repeatedly shuts down within ten minutes of being turned on. The technician notices a loud clicking sound coming from inside the case.
Which of the following components should the technician check first?
explanation: A loud clicking sound combined with rapid thermal shutdown is characteristic of a failing CPU fan. When the CPU fan fails or malfunctions, the processor overheats within minutes and triggers thermal protection shutdown. The clicking sound indicates mechanical failure of the fan bearing. The CPU fan should be checked first as its failure directly causes the thermal shutdown symptom.

why.A: A faulty exhaust fan would contribute to overheating but would not produce the distinct clicking sound associated with mechanical bearing failure.
why.B: While failing capacitors can cause shutdown, they typically fail silently without making clicking sounds.
why.D: An intake fan failure would reduce cooling efficiency but would not produce the clicking sound characteristic of bearing failure.

prompt: Which of the following is related to the creation of a secured communication channel between workstations in different locations and is supported by credentials for authentication?
explanation: A VPN (Virtual Private Network) creates a secured communication channel between remote workstations or networks by encrypting data and routing it through a secure tunnel. VPNs use credentials for authentication to verify the identity of users or devices before establishing the secure connection. This technology allows secure communication over untrusted networks like the internet between different physical locations.

why.A: DHCP is a protocol for automatic IP address assignment, not for creating secured communication channels.
why.B: CNAME is a DNS record type used for domain aliasing, not for secured communication channels.
why.C: VLAN is a network segmentation technology that creates logical networks on a single physical switch, not secured channels between different locations.

prompt: Which of the following allows for a beam of light to transmit data through a flexible cable?
explanation: Single-mode fiber uses a beam of light to transmit data through a flexible cable. This is the defining characteristic of fiber optic technology, where light pulses travel through a thin glass or plastic core to carry data at extremely high speeds over long distances.

why.A: Coaxial cables use electrical signals through a copper conductor, not light.
why.B: HDMI is a digital video/audio interface that uses electrical signals, not light transmission.
why.C: Thunderbolt is a high-speed interface standard that uses electrical signals over copper or optical paths, but is not primarily defined by light beam transmission through flexible cable.

prompt: An IT specialist is setting up a new. custom computer. The specialist wants to minimize the number of power cables to keep the internal components organized and uncluttered.
Which of the following power supply types should the specialist use?
explanation: A modular power supply allows the technician to connect only the necessary power cables to components, minimizing cable clutter inside the case. Non-modular supplies come with all cables permanently attached, whereas modular supplies have detachable cables that connect only as needed.

why.B: Redundant power supplies provide backup power but do not reduce the number of cables.
why.C: Linear power supplies are a type of voltage regulator design and do not address cable management.
why.D: External power supplies are outside the case and are typically used for peripherals, not internal component organization.

prompt: A company policy change requires all computers to be encrypted.
Which of the following technologies should a technician configure to meet this new requirement?
explanation: TPM (Trusted Platform Module) is a security chip that manages encryption keys and enables full disk encryption on computers. It stores cryptographic keys securely and works with BitLocker or similar encryption software to meet data encryption requirements.

why.A: NVMe is a storage interface protocol and does not provide encryption functionality.
why.B: RISC is a processor architecture type and is unrelated to data encryption.
why.C: ARM is a processor architecture and does not provide encryption capabilities.

prompt: A company wants to use cloud services with the requirement that data will reside on physical hardware that will not be shared with other companies.
Which of the following meets this requirement?
explanation: Dedicated resources in cloud services means the physical hardware is exclusively allocated to one company and is not shared with other organizations. This meets the requirement that data resides on non-shared physical infrastructure.

why.B: Elasticity refers to the ability to scale resources up or down dynamically and does not address hardware sharing.
why.C: Hybrid cloud combines on-premises and cloud resources but does not guarantee dedicated physical hardware.
why.D: SaaS is a software delivery model and does not provide control over physical hardware allocation.

prompt: A user connects a company-issued laptop to a 4K TV but can only get 1080p resolution on the TV. The technician confirms that the laptop is capable of producing a 4K output.
Which of the following the most likely cause of the issue?

options.text: The TV firmware is out of date.
The HDMI cable version is incorrect.
The laptop firmware is not current.
The CPU cannot keep up with the transcoding.

answerText: The HDMI cable version is incorrect.
explanation: Different HDMI cable versions support different bandwidth capabilities; older HDMI cables may not support the bandwidth required for 4K resolution. An HDMI 2.0 or newer cable is needed for 4K, while older versions like HDMI 1.4 may only support up to 1080p at certain refresh rates.

why.A: TV firmware being out of date could affect features, but the TV is displaying 1080p correctly, suggesting it is functioning properly.
why.C: Laptop firmware updates typically do not affect video output capability if the hardware is already 4K-capable.
why.D: CPU transcoding is not the bottleneck; the issue is at the cable/interface level preventing 4K data transmission.

prompt: Which of the following is an isolated virtual machine?
explanation: A sandbox is an isolated virtual machine or environment where applications run in complete isolation from the rest of the system, preventing any changes or malicious activity from affecting the host system or other applications.

why.B: A hypervisor is the software that creates and manages virtual machines, not an isolated VM itself.
why.C: A container is a lightweight virtualization method but shares the host OS kernel and is not as completely isolated as a sandbox.
why.D: VDI (Virtual Desktop Infrastructure) refers to virtual desktops delivered to users, not specifically an isolated test environment.

prompt: A user cannot see the office multifunction printer in their laptop's print options. They have printed to the device in the past successfully. The user’s laptop is connected to the guest wireless network. Other users on both wireless and wired computers can see and print to the printer.
Which of the following will fix the issue?

options.text: Power cycle the printer to refresh connectivity
Download the printer driver from the manufacturer's website
Connect the laptop to the corporate Wi-Fi

answerText: Connect the laptop to the corporate Wi-Fi
explanation: The user is connected to the guest wireless network, which is typically isolated from the corporate network where the multifunction printer resides. Connecting to the corporate Wi-Fi will allow the laptop to access the same network segment as the printer, making it visible and printable.

why.A: Power cycling the printer would not resolve a network isolation issue since other users can already see and print to it.
why.B: Resetting the wireless access point would not fix the printer visibility issue caused by the guest network isolation.
why.C: The printer driver is unlikely to be the issue since the user has printed successfully before and other users can see the printer.

prompt: A technician receives a notification after a network outage that indicates the printer is not reachable.
Which of the following printer settings should the technician implement to prevent this issue in the future?
explanation: Assigning a static IP address to the printer ensures it maintains the same IP address after network outages or restarts. This allows the notification system and other network
management tools to reliably locate the printer, preventing the 'not reachable' alerts that occur when DHCP reassigns a different IP.

why.A: A gateway is a network device for routing between networks and does not address printer reachability after outages.
why.C: APIPA (Automatic Private IP Addressing) is a fallback mechanism that assigns a link-local IP when DHCP fails, but it does not provide reliable, consistent addressing for network monitoring.
why.D: DHCP assigns IP addresses dynamically, which means the printer's IP could change after a network outage, causing reachability issues.

prompt: Which of the following network technologies is used for the operation of physical access control systems?
explanation: RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) is the standard technology used in physical access control systems for badge readers, key fobs, and credential verification. It enables wireless identification and authentication of users attempting to access secured areas. 802.1X is an authentication protocol, VPN is for remote network access, and GPS is for location tracking—none are used for physical access control operations.

why.A: 802.1X is a network authentication protocol, not used for physical door/gate access control.
why.B: VPN is used for secure remote network connections, not physical access control.
why.C: GPS is a location tracking technology, not relevant to physical access control systems.

prompt: A technician wants to evaluate several desktop Linux OSs simultaneously.
Which of the following is the best way to accomplish this task?
explanation: A hypervisor is the correct choice for simultaneously running multiple desktop Linux operating systems on a single computer. Hypervisors (Type 1 or Type 2) allow creation and management of multiple virtual machines, each running its own independent OS instance. Containers share a host OS kernel and are lighter-weight but not ideal for running different complete desktop OSs. Sandboxes isolate single applications, and VDI is a centralized desktop delivery solution rather than a local multi-OS evaluation tool.

why.A: Containers share a kernel and are designed for application isolation, not for running multiple complete desktop operating systems.
why.B: Sandboxes isolate individual applications, not entire operating systems.
why.D: VDI (Virtual Desktop Infrastructure) is a centralized solution for remote desktop delivery, not for local simultaneous OS evaluation.

prompt: A user asks a technician for assistance with a printer that has stopped printing. The user states that the print jobs are generated from a website and are difficult to re-create.
When the technician remotes into the user's computer, they can see many jobs in the queue. The issue persists after the user performs a hard reset of the printer.
Which of the following will most likely fix the issue?

options.text: Restarting the print spooler service on the local computer
Deleting all the jobs and having the user restart their computer
Making sure the printer is using the latest PCL driver
Updating the manufacturer's firmware on the printer

answerText: Restarting the print spooler service on the local
explanation: computer

The print spooler service manages the print queue on the local computer. When many jobs accumulate and fail to process even after a printer reset, the spooler service itself is likely corrupted or stuck. Restarting the print spooler clears the stuck queue and resets the service, allowing new jobs to process correctly. This is the most direct fix when print jobs are queued but not being sent to the printer.

why.B: Simply deleting jobs and restarting the computer may temporarily work but doesn't address the underlying spooler service issue.
why.C: PCL driver updates would not resolve jobs already stuck in the queue; the issue is queue management, not driver compatibility.
why.D: Firmware updates on the printer are unnecessary when the hard reset was already performed and the issue is job processing, not printer functionality.

prompt: A user reports that a laptop runs very slowly when documents are opened and saved. The user got the laptop within the past year. A technician finds the following specifications for the laptop:
•  Intel Core i5-1235U
•  Windows 11 Home
•  Intel Iris Xe Graphics
1TB 7200RPM 16GB: 2 x 8GB DDR4 2666
The technician thinks a minor upgrade should solve the slow performance issue.
Which of the following components should the technician install?
explanation: The laptop specifications show a 7200RPM mechanical hard drive as the bottleneck. For document operations (opening/saving), disk I/O speed is critical. Upgrading to a 2.5" SATA SSD would dramatically improve performance for file operations. The CPU (i5-1235U) and RAM (16GB DDR4) are adequate for document work. A gaming GPU is unnecessary, an i7 CPU offers marginal gains for this use case, and 64GB RAM is excessive for document editing.

why.A: A gaming GPU is not relevant to document opening and saving performance.
why.B: An i7 CPU would provide minimal performance gains for document operations; the bottleneck is storage speed, not processing power.
why.C: 64GB RAM is excessive for document editing and would not address the real performance bottleneck of a slow mechanical drive.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of SaaS?
explanation: Videoconferencing is a classic example of SaaS (Software as a Service) where the application is delivered over the internet and managed by the provider (e.g., Zoom, Microsoft Teams). Users access it through a browser or client without installing or maintaining software. Managed VDI is IaaS/DaaS, hosted databases are IaaS/DBaaS, and hypervisors are infrastructure components—none are consumer-facing SaaS applications.

why.B: Managed VDI is a Desktop-as-a-Service (DaaS) or Infrastructure-as-a-Service offering, not SaaS.
why.C: A hosted database is a Database-as-a-Service (DBaaS), which falls under IaaS, not SaaS.
why.D: A hypervisor is infrastructure-level virtualization technology, not a SaaS application.

prompt: A computer is experiencing random shutdowns. A technician notices that the fans on the computer work but are noisy. The CPU temperature is about 122°F (50°C) when the computer is started but rises to 208°F (98°C) when applications are opened.
Which of the following would most likely fix this issue?

options.text: Adding more RAM to the computer

explanation: The CPU temperature climbing to 98°C under load indicates inadequate heat dissipation from the CPU to the cooling system. While the fans are running (though noisy), a better heat sink with improved thermal conductivity and surface area would transfer heat more efficiently from the CPU to the fans. This addresses the thermal bottleneck causing random shutdowns due to thermal throttling or emergency shutoffs.

why.A: The power supply is not related to CPU temperature issues; random shutdowns from heat are thermal, not power-related.
why.C: Fan settings adjustment won't help if the heat sink itself isn't transferring heat adequately to the fans.
why.D: Adding RAM does not affect CPU cooling or thermal management.

prompt: A technician is troubleshooting an HDMI over Ethernet solution. The network link lights on the transmitter and receiver are both active. The TV that is connected to the receiver unit is getting audio, but video is intermittently flashing.
Which of the following should the technician check next to find the source of the issue?
explanation: Intermittent video flashing with audio working and active network link lights indicates a signal integrity issue. Poor network cable termination causes intermittent packet loss, affecting the video stream while audio (which uses lower bandwidth) continues. Since link lights are active but data integrity is compromised, checking cable termination, connector seating, and cable quality is the logical next troubleshooting step.

why.A: The HDMI source isn't the issue since audio is successfully received, ruling out source-side problems.
why.B: PoE power would cause complete failure, not intermittent video flashing with audio working.
why.C: TV firmware would not cause intermittent video issues; it would cause consistent problems or affect both audio and video equally.

prompt: A customer reports that internet browsing on their smartphone is fast at the beginning of the month but significantly slows down toward the end of the month. A technician examines the phone and finds multiple free cloud backup services running, with several gigabytes of personal data spread across each. Data availability is important to the customer.
Which of the following is the best way to resolve the customer's issue?

options.text: Disabling all cloud backup services except one
Installing an additional SD card for photos and videos
Expanding the cache storage to consolidate data
Configuring data synchronization only over Wi-Fi connections

answerText: Configuring data synchronization only over Wi-Fi
explanation: connections

The customer's issue is that multiple cloud backup services are continuously syncing gigabytes of data over cellular throughout the month, consuming the data limit. Configuring synchronization to occur only over Wi-Fi prevents cellular data consumption while maintaining data availability through Wi-Fi-based backups. This directly addresses the root cause without disabling important backups or requiring hardware additions.

why.A: Disabling cloud services reduces redundancy and compromises data availability, which the customer values.
why.B: An SD card doesn't solve the cloud sync problem; backups would still consume cellular data throughout the month.
why.C: Expanding cache storage does nothing to prevent cloud synchronization from consuming cellular bandwidth.

prompt: A user reports slow performance when saving documents locally on a computer. A technician reviews the logs and notices entries showing S.M.A.R.T. errors.
Which of the following actions should the technician take next?

options.text: Install a heat sink on the hard drive.

explanation: S.M.A.R.T. (Self-Monitoring, Analysis and Reporting Technology) errors indicate imminent or actual hard drive failure. When S.M.A.R.T. errors appear in logs, the drive is experiencing mechanical or electrical degradation and should be replaced before complete failure occurs and data is lost.
