why.D: Emulation simulates hardware at instruction level and is much slower and less efficient than hypervisor-based virtualization for running full operating systems.

prompt: A company wants to optimize its hardware usage by running multiple operating systems concurrently on a single physical server.
Which of the following concepts achieves this goal?
explanation: Host-based virtualization (also called Type 2 hypervisor virtualization) enables multiple operating systems to run concurrently on a single physical server by virtualizing hardware resources. This directly addresses optimizing hardware usage by consolidating workloads that would otherwise require separate physical servers.

why.B: Public cloud services provide computing resources remotely but do not directly involve running multiple OS instances on a single server—the servers are managed by the cloud provider.
why.C: High-availability clustering provides redundancy and failover capabilities but does not optimize hardware usage by running multiple OS instances concurrently on one server.
why.D: Software as a service is a cloud delivery model for applications, not a technology for running multiple operating systems on a single physical server.
why.E: Load balancing distributes traffic across multiple systems but does not involve running multiple operating systems concurrently on a single physical machine.

prompt: A network printer consistently produces faint printouts. Users report that the issue persists across different computers and print jobs.
Which of the following steps should the technician take first?
explanation: Faint printouts consistently across multiple computers and print jobs is a classic symptom of a depleted or low-quality toner cartridge. Since the issue persists regardless of the source or content being printed, the toner cartridge should be replaced first as it is the most common cause of faint output and is the simplest troubleshooting step.

why.A: Printer calibration addresses color accuracy and alignment issues, not the brightness or darkness of print output related to toner supply.
why.C: If drivers were the problem, the issue would likely manifest inconsistently or with specific computer/job combinations, not universally across all devices and jobs.
why.D: Fuser temperature adjustment is an advanced maintenance step and would not typically be the first troubleshooting action for consistently faint output across all jobs.

prompt: A user turns on their laptop. The keyboard lights up. but the screen is black even after the user restarts the laptop.
Which of the following should a technician do next to troubleshoot the issue?

options.text: Connect the laptop to an external monitor.

answerText: Connect the laptop to an external monitor.
explanation: Connecting the laptop to an external monitor is the most logical first troubleshooting step when the keyboard lights up but the screen remains black. This determines whether the issue is with the display/video output (internal screen failure) or with the laptop's core functionality. If the external monitor works, the problem is isolated to the internal display; if not, deeper hardware issues are indicated.

why.B: Removing the device bezel is invasive disassembly that should not be performed before basic troubleshooting determines whether the display or other components are faulty.
why.C: The keyboard lighting indicates the laptop is powered on; if the issue persisted after restart, a charger connection is unlikely to resolve a black screen problem.
why.D: Replacing the entire laptop is premature and wasteful before performing basic diagnostics to identify whether the issue is the display, graphics, or other components.

prompt: A user reports that the office inkjet printer is making smudges on the printed pages.
Which of the following tasks would best resolve the issue?
explanation: Smudges on printed pages from an inkjet printer are typically caused by dried or clogged print cartridge heads that deposit ink irregularly. Cleaning the cartridge heads removes dried ink buildup and restores proper ink flow, resolving smudging issues. This is a standard maintenance procedure for inkjet printers.

why.A: A maintenance kit is a set of replacement parts (drums, rollers, etc.) used for preventive maintenance on laser printers, not relevant to inkjet smudging.
why.C: Paper jams would cause printing to stop or produce crumpled output, not smudges across multiple pages.
why.D: The fuser is a laser printer component that applies toner by heat; inkjet printers do not use fusers and this is not applicable to the issue.

prompt: Marketing department users report network performance degradation in the morning and early afternoon, but sales and customer service department users do not report any issues. All structured cabling is Cat 5e. All departments are connected to a core switch. The running network configuration shows the following:
Which of the following is the most likely cause of the performance issues?

options.text: The marketing department subnet has an error.
The structured Cat 5e cabling is outdated.
The interfaces are configured with incorrect IP addresses.
The marketing department interface is running at 10/100.

answerText: The marketing department interface is running at
explanation: The marketing department interface (gigabitEthernet0/3) is configured with 'speed auto' and 'duplex auto', which means it can negotiate down to 10/100 Mbps speeds. In contrast, the Sales and CustomerService interfaces are explicitly set to 'speed 1000' (gigabit). When an interface falls back to 10/100 Mbps due to auto-negotiation issues or mismatched configurations, it creates a significant bottleneck compared to the gigabit connections of other departments. This would cause performance degradation specifically during times of higher usage (morning and early afternoon when marketing staff are most active), while other departments experience no issues because they have dedicated gigabit connectivity. The auto-negotiation setting on the marketing interface is the most likely culprit for the intermittent performance problems.

why.A: All three department subnets use valid Class C IP addresses (192.168.1.0/24) with appropriate host addresses; there is no subnet configuration error.
why.B: While Cat 5e is older cabling, it still supports gigabit Ethernet speeds up to 100 meters and all interfaces except marketing are running at 1000 Mbps successfully, so the cabling is not the primary cause.
why.C: The IP addresses are correctly configured within the same subnet (192.168.1.0/24) with proper netmask (255.255.255.0); there is no IP address configuration error causing the performance issue.

prompt: A user needs cellular internet connectivity for their laptop without using an external device.
Which of the following technologies can the user use on their laptop to achieve this connection?
explanation: A SIM card (Subscriber Identity Module) embedded or inserted into a laptop enables cellular internet connectivity by connecting to cellular networks (4G, 5G, etc.) without requiring an external device. Some modern laptops include built-in cellular modems that work with SIM cards for native mobile broadband connectivity.

why.A: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless protocol designed for device pairing and peripheral connectivity, not for internet connectivity.
why.B: A hotspot is a feature that shares an existing internet connection from another device; it does not provide the initial cellular internet connection to the laptop itself.
why.D: NFC (Near Field Communication) is a short-range wireless technology for data exchange between devices in close proximity, not for internet connectivity.

prompt: A company wants to get the fastest network speeds possible between nearby locations. If all technologies are available, which of the following connection types should the company use?
explanation: Fiber optic cables provide the fastest network speeds available among common connection types, with speeds often exceeding 1 Gbps and capable of reaching 10+ Gbps. Fiber is the best choice for the fastest network speeds between nearby locations when all technologies are available.

why.B: DSL (Digital Subscriber Line) provides much slower speeds than fiber, typically ranging from 5-35 Mbps, making it significantly inferior for high-speed needs.
why.C: Satellite connections have high latency and lower bandwidth compared to fiber, making them unsuitable for the fastest speeds and generally used only when terrestrial options are unavailable.
why.D: Coaxial cable (cable internet) is faster than DSL but still slower than fiber optic, typically offering speeds up to 1 Gbps while fiber can exceed this significantly.

prompt: Which of the following describes an advantage of traditional HDDs over SSDs?
explanation: Traditional HDDs (Hard Disk Drives) offer significantly higher storage capacity per dollar than SSDs. While SSDs are faster and more efficient, HDDs remain the more cost-effective solution for large-capacity storage, making this the primary advantage of HDDs in modern computing.

why.A: SSDs have faster data access speeds than HDDs due to no mechanical moving parts; this is an advantage of SSDs, not HDDs.
why.B: SSDs are more energy efficient than HDDs because they have no moving mechanical components; HDDs consume more power for motor and actuator movement.
why.D: SSDs are lighter and more compact than HDDs due to their solid-state design; HDDs are bulkier and heavier due to spinning platters and mechanical components.

prompt: After a laptop screen has been replaced, the laptop is having Wi-Fi connectivity issues. No SSIDs are discovered. Bluetooth and Ethernet are working.
Which of the following should a technician investigate first?
explanation: After a laptop screen replacement, the Wi-Fi antenna is the most likely component to have been accidentally disconnected or damaged during disassembly. Laptop antennas are typically routed through the display bezel and reconnected during reassembly. Since Bluetooth and Ethernet work, the wireless card itself is likely functional, making the antenna connection the first thing to investigate.

why.A: The wireless card would likely show as disabled or absent in device manager; it wouldn't selectively fail to discover SSIDs if working.
why.C: An access point issue would affect all devices, not just this one laptop after a screen replacement.
why.D: The network interface card for Ethernet is working, so the motherboard connectivity is proven functional.
why.E: A motherboard failure would likely cause more systemic issues beyond just Wi-Fi, and would have existed before the screen replacement.

prompt: Which of the following is used to assign an IP address to a network PC?
explanation: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) is the service that automatically assigns IP
addresses to network devices. It is the standard protocol used for dynamic IP address allocation on most networks.

why.A: VLAN is used to segment networks logically, not to assign IP addresses.
why.B: DNS translates domain names to IP addresses; it does not assign addresses to devices.
why.D: TCP is a transport layer protocol for reliable data transmission, not for IP address assignment.

prompt: Which of the following offers access to business productivity applications for a recurring fee?
explanation: SaaS (Software as a Service) provides business productivity applications like Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and Salesforce delivered over the cloud on a subscription basis, allowing users to pay a recurring fee for access.

why.B: DaaS (Desktop as a Service) provides virtualized desktop environments, not specifically productivity applications.
why.C: PaaS (Platform as a Service) provides development platforms and tools, not end-user productivity applications.
why.D: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) provides virtualized computing resources like servers and storage, not applications.

prompt: A support technician for a small office is asked to improve the signal quality of the wireless network. An employee located in Office 1 reports poor Wi-Fi performance, particularly during certain times of the day.
The office has two access points, and each access point has a coverage of 2,000 sq ft (186 sq m), while the total office space is approximately 3,000 sq ft (279 sq m).
Additionally, the management team requests that any electronics should be located strategically to minimize signal interference.
INSTRUCTIONS
Click the X in the upper right comer of each device to remove it from its current location.
Click on a ? around the office to add a device to that location.
Devices should be moved to the appropriate locations in order to satisfy the above requirements, and all devices will be placed around the office.
summary: Relocate network devices and sources of interference to improve Wi-Fi signal coverage and minimize performance degradation in the office.

pairs.match: Hallway (target at the Office 3 / Conference room end)

steps: 1. Identify that the office requires two access points to cover 3,000 sq ft, with each providing 2,000 sq ft coverage.
2. Position the first access point in the Hallway to serve Office 1 and surrounding areas, addressing the poor signal complaint.
3. Position the second access point in Office 3 to extend coverage to that area and ensure overlapping but complementary coverage.
4. Move the Microwave away from office areas to the Security room since microwave ovens emit 2.4 GHz radiation that interferes with Wi-Fi.
5. Move the Walkie Talkies away from office areas to the Conference room since radio devices can cause interference on wireless networks.

The solution addresses both coverage and interference requirements. By placing access points in the Hallway and Office 3, coverage extends throughout the 3,000 sq ft office space with strategic positioning to reach Office 1 where poor performance was reported. Simultaneously, the two main sources of electromagnetic interference—the Microwave and Walkie Talkies—are relocated to isolated areas (Security room and Conference room) away from the primary work spaces, eliminating the interference that was likely degrading signal quality during certain times of the day when these devices were in use near the offices.

prompt: Which of the following is a way to synchronize the clocks across all devices in an environment?
explanation: NTP (Network Time Protocol) is specifically designed to synchronize clocks across all devices in a network environment. It ensures consistent time across servers, workstations, and network devices, which is critical for logging, security, and system operations.

why.A: DHCP lease duration affects IP address assignment timing, not clock synchronization.
why.B: DNS servers translate domain names to IP addresses; they do not synchronize system clocks.
why.C: HTTP servers serve web content and have no role in time synchronization.

prompt: Which of the following cable types requires a user to manually turn the connector in a clockwise direction in order to securely attach the cable?
explanation: Coaxial cables use BNC or F-connectors that require a clockwise twist motion to securely attach. This is the standard method for connecting coaxial cables in RF applications, cable television, and legacy networking.

why.A: Ethernet connectors (RJ45) use a push-click mechanism, not a clockwise twist.
why.B: HDMI connectors use a friction-fit push design without twisting.
why.C: Fiber-optic connectors vary (SC, LC, ST) but typically use push/pull or snap mechanisms, not clockwise twisting.
why.D: Serial connectors (DB-9, DB-25) use threaded collars that screw, which is different from a simple clockwise turn of the connector itself.

prompt: A technician installs a new workgroup MFP in a small office with a DHCP address. Immediately after the MFP is installed, office IoT devices using Wi-Fi experience connectivity issues. The office has a single Wi-Fi access point, and the IoT devices can only operate on the 2.4GHz spectrum.
Which of the following should the technician do next to troubleshoot the issue?

options.text: Enable the Wi-Fi Direct feature on the MFP.
Configure the MFP with WPA3 instead of WPA2.
Connect the printer to the network using Ethernet.
Assign a unique static IP address.

answerText: Connect the printer to the network using Ethernet.
explanation: The MFP is likely consuming significant 2.4GHz Wi-Fi bandwidth, causing interference with the IoT devices that operate exclusively on that band. Connecting the printer to Ethernet removes it from the wireless spectrum, freeing 2.4GHz bandwidth for the IoT devices. This is the most direct troubleshooting step to isolate the problem.

why.A: Wi-Fi Direct would add another wireless connection, worsening the congestion problem rather than solving it.
why.B: Changing security protocols would not address bandwidth congestion issues caused by the MFP.
why.D: Assigning a static IP does not resolve Wi-Fi bandwidth contention problems.

prompt: A computer with two redundant drives is displaying an error:
SMART failure predicted: Drive 1 A technician notes that a spare drive is not available and the computer is currently functioning normally.
Which of the following should the technician do next?
explanation: When a SMART failure is predicted on a redundant drive system with no spare available, the technician should immediately request a replacement drive. This ensures the spare is available before the drive fails, maintaining redundancy. The system is functioning now, so there is time to order a replacement rather than taking immediate disruptive action.

why.A: Immediately removing the drive would destroy redundancy and cause system failure if the remaining drive fails.
why.C: Rebuilding the array with a failed drive would be impossible and could cause data loss.
why.D: Restoring the base image is unnecessary when the problem is hardware failure, not software corruption.

prompt: Which of the following networking hardware devices is primarily used to connect different network segments and forward data based on MAC addresses?
explanation: A switch is a Layer 2 device that connects different network segments and forwards data frames based on MAC addresses. It learns and maintains a MAC address table to intelligently forward frames only to the appropriate ports.

why.A: A router operates at Layer 3 and forwards data based on IP addresses, not MAC addresses.
why.C: A modem modulates and demodulates signals for internet connectivity; it does not forward data based on MAC addresses.
why.D: A firewall filters traffic based on security rules, not MAC addresses, and operates at higher layers.

prompt: An administrator is configuring a bare-metal server to host several virtual machines.
Which of the following should the administrator use to complete this task?
explanation: A hypervisor is the software layer that enables virtualization by abstracting physical hardware and allowing multiple virtual machines to run on a single bare-metal server. This is the foundational technology required to host VMs on physical hardware.

why.A: VLAN is a network segmentation technology, not for hosting virtual machines.
why.C: VDI (Virtual Desktop Infrastructure) is a use case for virtualization, not the technology that enables it.
why.D: RDP is a remote access protocol, not a virtualization platform.
why.E: Containers are a lightweight alternative to VMs but don't provide the same hardware abstraction needed for this scenario.

prompt: Which of the following is used to expose the wires in an unshielded twisted pair?
explanation: A cable stripper is the tool specifically designed to remove the outer insulation from unshielded twisted pair (UTP) cables to expose the individual wires inside. This is a necessary first step before terminating the cable.

why.A: A loopback plug is used for testing network connectivity, not exposing wires.
why.B: A punchdown tool is used to secure wires into terminals after they're exposed, not to expose them.
why.C: A crimper is used to attach connectors to cables after stripping, not to strip the cable.

prompt: Which of the following wireless technologies has the most range but is susceptible to more interference?
explanation: Wi-Fi 5 operates in the 5GHz frequency band which has greater range capability than NFC and Bluetooth, but the 5GHz band is more susceptible to interference from obstacles and competing signals compared to lower frequencies, and it doesn't penetrate walls as
effectively as 2.4GHz Wi-Fi.

why.A: NFC has very short range (typically a few centimeters), not the most range.
why.B: Bluetooth has limited range compared to Wi-Fi and is generally less susceptible to interference.
why.D: Infrared has very short range and doesn't penetrate obstacles at all.

prompt: A technician is setting up a SOHO router. The environment requires DHCP to be disabled.
Which of the following address types must the technician configure?
explanation: When DHCP is disabled, the technician must manually assign static IP addresses to devices so they have a fixed, non-changing IP configuration. Static addressing is the only viable alternative to DHCP in network environments.

why.B: Dynamic addressing requires DHCP to assign addresses automatically.
why.C: Public vs. private relates to address classes, not the DHCP vs. manual configuration choice.
why.D: APIPA is an automatic fallback mechanism when DHCP fails, not a configured replacement for DHCP.

prompt: A company's directory services server is located on premises.
Which of the following best describes the directory services infrastructure?
explanation: An on-premises directory services server that is owned and operated by the company internally represents a private cloud infrastructure, where computing resources are dedicated exclusively to that organization and not shared with others.

why.A: Hybrid cloud involves a mix of on-premises and public cloud resources, not purely on-premises.
why.C: Public cloud is hosted by third parties and shared across multiple organizations.
why.D: Community cloud is shared among specific organizations with common interests, not exclusive to one company.

prompt: After a technician installs a new network printer, the technician discovers that one of the printer features is not available.
Which of the following should the technician do first?

options.text: Connect the printer with a USB cable.

explanation: When a newly installed printer feature is unavailable, the first troubleshooting step should be to update the firmware, as missing features often result from outdated firmware that doesn't support all hardware capabilities or requires driver/firmware updates to activate.

why.B: Contacting the manufacturer should be done after attempting basic troubleshooting steps.
why.C: IPv6 enablement is not typically related to missing printer features.
why.D: Using a USB cable instead of network connection doesn't enable features; it may actually limit them.

prompt: A user’s monitor shows strange colored lines and flickers when adjusting the brightness. The user requires the device for daily professional tasks.
Which of the following should a technician do to effectively address the screen issue, given cost and urgency considerations?

options.text: Suggest the user use a secondary monitor for essential tasks.
Conduct a factory reset to eliminate software issues
Install a screen protector to minimize flickering.
Check for loose connections on the display.

answerText: Check for loose connections on the display.
explanation: Strange colored lines and flickering when adjusting brightness typically indicate a loose or faulty video cable connection. Checking for loose connections is the first troubleshooting step and is the most cost-effective and quickest solution before considering hardware replacement.

why.A: Using a secondary monitor temporarily works around the problem but doesn't address the root cause.
why.B: A factory reset won't fix hardware connection issues and wastes time on unnecessary troubleshooting.
why.C: A screen protector won't address hardware flickering or display signal problems.

prompt: Which of the following technologies uses smartphones to allow contactless entry to secure areas?
explanation: NFC (Near Field Communication) is specifically designed for contactless transactions and secure access. Modern smartphones with NFC capability can be used as digital credentials for contactless entry to secure areas when properly configured.

why.B: Infrared requires line-of-sight and is not used for contactless building access.
why.C: RFID requires specialized RFID tags and readers, not standard smartphone integration for secure access.
why.D: Bluetooth has longer range but is not standardized for secure contactless building access in the way NFC is.

prompt: An administrator must configure a server that prioritizes data availability. Because the server will be accessed by many users, the administrator must also consider performance.
Which of the following RAID levels best meets these requirements within a single array?
explanation: RAID 10 (1+0) combines the benefits of RAID 1 (mirroring for redundancy and read performance) and RAID 0 (striping for performance). It provides excellent data availability through mirroring while delivering superior performance through striping across multiple mirror pairs. This makes it ideal for high-availability, high-performance environments within a single array.

why.A: RAID 1 offers good availability but limited performance scaling compared to RAID 10.
why.B: RAID 2 is obsolete and rarely used in modern systems.
why.C: RAID 5 provides adequate performance and redundancy but slower write performance than RAID 10 due to parity calculations.

prompt: An employee's corporate phone is experiencing connectivity issues. The user is unable to access the internet, send emails, or use business applications outside the office. The device is not in airplane mode, and Wi-Fi is turned off.
Which of the following is the most likely cause of the issue?

options.text: The SIM is malfunctioning and needs to be replaced.
The user has exceeded the phone's mobile data plan.
The phone is missing security updates.

answerText: The user has exceeded the phone's mobile data plan.
explanation: The user cannot access internet, email, or business applications outside the office, but the phone is not in airplane mode and Wi-Fi is off. This indicates a cellular/mobile data issue. Since the device is functioning normally otherwise, the most likely cause is that the user has exceeded their mobile data plan limit, which carriers typically respond to by throttling
or blocking data access. A malfunctioning SIM would affect calls as well, SSID issues are irrelevant with Wi-Fi off, and missing security updates wouldn't cause total connectivity loss.

why.A: A malfunctioning SIM would typically also prevent calls and texts, not just data.
why.C: SSID settings are irrelevant since Wi-Fi is turned off on the device.
why.D: Missing security updates would not cause total loss of cellular connectivity.

prompt: Which of the following display technologies is known for offering the highest contrast ratios?
explanation: OLED (Organic Light-Emitting Diode) displays produce the highest contrast ratios of all consumer display technologies because each pixel emits its own light and can be individually turned off completely, resulting in true blacks. This creates theoretically infinite contrast ratios, far superior to LCD, LED, or QLED technologies which all rely on backlighting.

why.A: LCD displays use backlighting and cannot achieve true black, limiting contrast ratio.
why.B: LED is a backlighting technology for LCDs and has similar contrast limitations.
why.D: QLED uses quantum dots to improve color and brightness but still relies on backlighting, resulting in lower contrast than OLED.

prompt: A busy network printer is producing faded printouts after a technician performed maintenance on the printer several months ago. The technician now replaces the toner cartridge, but the issue persists.
Which of the following should the technician check next?
explanation: Faded printouts that persist after toner cartridge replacement indicate a problem with the imaging process itself, not the toner supply. The drum unit is the component that holds the electrostatic image before toner is applied. If the drum was damaged or worn during the previous maintenance, it would cause faded output regardless of toner quality. Checking the drum unit for wear or damage is the logical next diagnostic step.

why.A: Firmware version issues would typically cause other symptoms like print quality modes not responding, not persistent fading.
why.B: Paper type would affect texture and finish but not cause fading after a maintenance event.
why.D: Print resolution settings would affect clarity and sharpness but not cause the specific symptom of fading across all prints.

prompt: After several workstations received OS updates, users report that their network speeds have dropped. A technician verifies that the network speeds on other workstations are fine.
Which of the following would most likely solve the issue on the updated workstations?

options.text: Rolling back to the previous driver

answerText: Rolling back to the previous driver
explanation: Network speed drops occurred specifically after OS updates on affected workstations, while other workstations remain unaffected. This strongly suggests the issue is with a network driver that was updated or modified during the OS update process. Rolling back to the previous driver version would restore the prior functionality and is the most direct solution to a driver-related performance problem.

why.B: Replacing network cards is a hardware solution unnecessary for a driver-related issue.
why.C: Restarting the router would affect all workstations, but only updated ones have the problem.
why.D: Switching to IPv6 would not resolve speed issues and is unlikely to be related to OS updates affecting specific workstations.

prompt: A user’s smartphone has stopped connecting to corporate Wi-Fi networks. The user has tried restarting the phone, but the issue persists. The device indicates full signal strength but fails to obtain an IP address during connection attempts. The user also notes that the smartphone can still connect to cellular data without any issues.
Which of the following is the most likely cause of the connectivity issue?
explanation: The smartphone shows full signal strength, can connect to cellular data, but fails to obtain an IP address when attempting to connect to corporate Wi-Fi. The inability to obtain an IP address specifically indicates a DHCP failure—the device can reach the network and authenticate but cannot receive addressing information. Cellular still works, ruling out antenna problems; full signal strength rules out weak signal; and the issue is specific to Wi-Fi, not a general firmware problem.

why.B: Outdated firmware would typically affect multiple connectivity types, not just Wi-Fi IP assignment.
why.C: A malfunctioning antenna would prevent connection entirely, not allow connection attempts that fail at DHCP.
why.D: Full signal strength is indicated, and if signal was insufficient, the device would not attempt connection.

prompt: A technician is migrating an application server to another server.
Which of the following DNS records should the technician create to ensure seamless connectivity?
explanation: When migrating an application server to another host, a CNAME (Canonical Name) record creates an alias that points the original server name to the new server's hostname. This ensures seamless connectivity because existing clients and applications can continue using the original server name without reconfiguration, while the CNAME transparently redirects to the new server location.

why.A: TXT records are used for text information and domain verification, not for server migration.
why.B: SPF records are for email authentication and spam prevention, not for application server connectivity.
why.C: DKIM records are for email digital signatures and authentication, not for server migration.

prompt: A company network is spread across multiple office branches that are located within the same postal code and connected using leased lines.
Which of the following best describes this network type?
explanation: A campus area network (CAN) connects multiple office locations within the same city or limited geographic area (same postal code) using leased lines or private connections. It is larger than a LAN but smaller and more localized than a WAN. The key descriptor is 'same postal code' with leased line connections, which is the defining characteristic of a CAN.

why.B: A metropolitan area network (MAN) typically covers a larger geographic area like an entire city, not just locations within the same postal code.
why.C: A local area network (LAN) is typically limited to a single building or office, not multiple branch locations.
why.D: A wide area network (WAN) spans large geographic distances like multiple cities or countries, exceeding the scope of same-postal-code locations.

prompt: A user wants to use a new laptop to play audio and video to an office projector, but the laptop does not have VGA or HDMI.
Which of the following adapters should the user buy?
explanation: USB-C to HDMI is the correct adapter because modern laptops without VGA or HDMI typically have USB-C ports, and USB-C supports video output via Alt Mode. This adapter allows the laptop to connect to a projector via HDMI. USB-C is the modern standard port found on contemporary laptops and supports multiple protocols including video transmission.

why.B: MicroUSB is rarely found on modern laptops and does not reliably support video output.
why.C: DisplayPort to VGA is backwards—while DisplayPort can output video, the laptop would need a DisplayPort input, not output, which is not mentioned.
why.D: DVI to HDMI does not solve the problem since the laptop lacks both DVI and HDMI ports.

prompt: Which of the following port numbers is used for NetBIOS?
explanation: Port 137 is used for NetBIOS Name Service, which is part of the NetBIOS protocol suite used for Windows networking and computer name resolution. NetBIOS operates on ports 137-139, with 137 specifically handling name service requests.

why.A: Port 110 is used for POP3 (email retrieval).
why.C: Port 143 is used for IMAP (email retrieval).
why.D: Port 445 is used for SMB (Server Message Block) over TCP, which is related but not NetBIOS itself.

prompt: Which of the following describes a virtualization concept that improves resource utilization by allowing multiple operating systems to run on a single physical server?
explanation: A virtual machine is the core virtualization concept that allows multiple complete operating systems to run on a single physical server with isolated resources and full OS capabilities. VMs are managed by hypervisors and represent the primary method for improving resource utilization through OS-level virtualization.

why.A: Containerization is lighter-weight and shares the host OS kernel rather than running full operating systems.
why.C: A hypervisor is the technology that enables virtualization but is not itself the concept of running multiple OSs.
why.D: Microservices architecture is a software design pattern unrelated to running multiple operating systems on one server.

prompt: Which of the following connector types would most likely be used to connect a fiber-optic cable to an SFP module?
explanation: LC (Lucent Connector) is the most common connector type used with SFP (Small Form-factor Pluggable) modules. LC connectors are compact, push-pull style connectors that
are the standard for high-density fiber-optic connections in modern networking equipment.

why.A: ST connectors are larger and older, typically used in legacy installations, not SFP modules.
why.B: SC connectors are larger than LC and less commonly paired with modern SFP modules.
why.C: FC connectors are threaded connectors primarily used in legacy equipment and telecommunications, not SFP modules.

prompt: A developer needs to isolate a testing VM in a Type 1 hypervisor from the other guests.
Which of the following does the administrator need to use to accomplish this task?
explanation: A sandbox is an isolated testing environment that prevents a guest VM from affecting other systems or accessing resources outside its controlled boundaries. This is the appropriate tool for isolating a testing VM in a Type 1 hypervisor to ensure it cannot interact with other production guests.

why.A: VDI (Virtual Desktop Infrastructure) is for delivering virtual desktops to users, not for isolating test VMs.
why.B: Containers are lightweight OS-level virtualization, not relevant to Type 1 hypervisor guest isolation.
why.C: A private cloud is an infrastructure deployment model, not a mechanism for isolating individual VMs.

prompt: A technician is building a custom CAD workstation with a high-end graphics card. The customer requests that the system has the highest possible stability.
Which of the following is the best choice for the power supply?
explanation: A redundant power supply provides the highest stability for a custom CAD workstation by offering failover capability—if one power supply fails, the other automatically takes over without system downtime. This is critical for expensive high-end graphics configurations where stability and uptime are paramount.

why.A: A UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) protects against outages but does not directly improve hardware stability.
why.C: A surge protector prevents damage from power spikes but does not enhance system stability or provide redundancy.
why.D: A modular power supply offers cable management benefits but provides no stability or redundancy advantages.

prompt: Which of the following tools would most likely be used to identify a cable's location in the network closet?
explanation: A toner probe (also called a tone generator and probe kit) is specifically designed to trace and locate cables in network closets. One end emits a tone on the cable, and the probe detects the tone to identify the cable's location—this is the industry-standard tool for cable identification.

why.A: A loopback plug is used for testing port functionality, not locating cables.
why.B: A crimper is used to attach connectors to cables, not to identify cable locations.
why.D: A network tap is used to monitor network traffic, not to physically locate cables in closets.

prompt: Which of the following is the best option to maintain a stable, tethered connection between a cell phone and a laptop?
explanation: USB provides the most stable and reliable tethered connection between a cell phone and laptop because it offers consistent power delivery, fast data transfer, and a dedicated physical connection that does not degrade with distance or interference. USB tethering maintains a reliable, wired connection ideal for sustained use.

why.A: Bluetooth is wireless and subject to range limitations and interference, making it less stable than USB.
why.C: Hotspot creates a wireless network rather than a direct tethered connection.
why.D: NFC (Near Field Communication) is for short-range wireless communication and does not support sustained data tethering.

prompt: A technician is troubleshooting a computer that fails to start and makes frequent, unexpected sounds. The monitor remains blank, and no OS loads.
Which of the following should the technician review first to diagnose this issue?
explanation: When a computer fails to start with unexpected sounds and a blank monitor, RAM issues are the most common cause of no POST codes or boot attempt. RAM modules can become unseated during handling or shipping, preventing the system from completing POST. While power supply voltages, thermal paste, and boot configuration are valid troubleshooting steps, they would typically result in different symptoms (no power, shutdown, or error codes). RAM is the first check because improper seating prevents any system initialization.

why.A: Power supply voltage issues would likely result in complete power loss or immediate shutdown, not frequent sounds with partial power.
why.B: Thermal paste issues cause overheating and shutdowns during operation, not failure to boot with no POST codes.
why.C: OS boot configuration issues occur after POST completes; this system is failing before or during POST.

prompt: Which of the following contains details about its manufacturer and is hardcoded?
explanation: A MAC (Media Access Control) address is hardcoded into network interface cards by the manufacturer. It contains the manufacturer's organizational unique identifier (OUI) in the first three octets, identifying who produced the NIC. This information is burned into the hardware during manufacturing and cannot be changed without special tools.

why.A: DSL is a connection technology type, not an address containing manufacturer details.
why.C: APIPA (Automatic Private IP Addressing) is dynamically assigned by the OS when DHCP fails, not hardcoded.
why.D: IP addresses are assigned by network administrators or DHCP servers, not hardcoded by manufacturers.

prompt: Which of the following is used to implement PoE?
explanation: A PoE injector is a device specifically designed to add power to Ethernet cables for

devices like IP cameras and wireless access points. It combines DC power with data on a single cable pair. While PoE switches can also deliver PoE, the injector is the primary device used to implement PoE in existing networks without replacing switches.

why.A: A modem converts ISP signals to usable internet, not related to PoE implementation.
why.B: Range extenders amplify wireless signals and do not implement PoE.
why.C: Media converters change signal types (fiber to copper) but do not add power to cables.

prompt: A technician replaces a motherboard in a desktop computer. Alter reassembling the system and turning it on, the computer tails to start, and no display output is shown. The power supply fan and case fans are working, but there are no beep codes or POST messages.
Which of the following should the technician do first to make the computer turn on properly?

options.text: Replace the power supply with a higher wattage unit.
Ensure that the CPU power connector is properly installed.

answerText: Ensure that the CPU power connector is properly
explanation: installed.

After a motherboard replacement, the most common cause of no POST codes or beep codes is an improperly connected CPU power connector. This 8-pin or 4-pin connector is essential for the CPU to operate. Without it properly seated, the system won't complete POST initialization, resulting in fans running but no startup sequence. This should be checked before memory, BIOS updates, or power supply replacement.

why.A: If the power supply were insufficient, the system would likely shut down or fail to power on completely, not run fans without POST.
why.C: BIOS updates are performed after POST succeeds; a new motherboard will boot with factory BIOS settings.
why.D: Memory issues typically produce beep codes or error messages; they would be checked after the CPU power connector.

prompt: Which of the following devices can provide combined data and power to hardwired VoIP phones in a small office?
explanation: A PoE switch is specifically designed to deliver both data and electrical power to networked devices over a single Ethernet cable. This is ideal for hardwired VoIP phones in a small office, eliminating the need for separate power cables and outlets. The switch handles both functions natively, making it the most efficient solution.

why.A: An injector is a single-port device; it would be impractical for multiple phones in an office.
why.C: An optical network terminal is used for fiber-to-copper conversion in ISP networks, not for office device powering.
why.D: A router provides network connectivity but typically does not supply PoE power to devices.

prompt: A company requires a storage solution that combines performance and redundancy for a main database server with high levels of read/write operations.
Which of the following storage configurations best meets these requirements?
explanation: RAID 10 (1+0) combines mirroring (RAID 1) and striping (RAID 0), providing both excellent performance through striping and redundancy through mirroring. It offers the best read/write performance with fault tolerance, making it ideal for high-performance database servers. It can sustain loss of one drive per mirror set without data loss.

why.A: RAID 0 offers performance but zero redundancy; a single drive failure results in total data loss.
why.B: RAID 5 provides redundancy but has slower write performance due to parity calculations, less ideal for high write operations.
why.C: RAID 6 provides redundancy but slower write performance than RAID 10 due to dual parity overhead.

prompt: A user's laptop keyboard is distorted and is no longer flat.
Which of the following components most likely tailed?
explanation: A swollen or distorted keyboard indicates a failed battery beneath it. Modern laptop batteries can swell due to internal chemical degradation, physically pushing up against the keyboard and warping it. This is a common sign of battery failure and poses a safety risk. The keyboard itself would not cause this warping pattern.

why.B: RAM failure would not affect the physical keyboard structure or cause visible distortion.
why.C: A failed keyboard might not function, but would not cause the keyboard to physically bulge or become non-flat.
why.D: An HDD failure would not cause physical deformation of the keyboard or any visible warping.

prompt: Which of the following types of RAM is typically used in servers?
explanation: ECC (Error-Correcting Code) RAM is the standard for server environments because it

detects and corrects single-bit memory errors automatically. This is critical for server reliability and data integrity in mission-critical applications. ECC RAM protects against data corruption caused by cosmic rays and electrical interference.

why.A: SODIMM is a small form factor for laptops and compact systems, not typical servers.
why.B: Rambus is an outdated RAM technology from the early 2000s, no longer used in modern servers.
why.C: DDR3 is a type of RAM but does not specify error correction; servers specifically require ECC-capable RAM regardless of DDR version.

prompt: A specialist needs to configure a computer so that it will not boot up using any non-trusted or unsigned external devices that are connected to the computer.
Which of the following should the specialist configure?
explanation: Secure Boot is a UEFI firmware feature that prevents the computer from booting using unsigned or untrusted external devices and bootloaders. It verifies the digital signatures of boot files before allowing the system to start, ensuring only trusted code executes during the boot process. This directly addresses the requirement to prevent booting from non-trusted external devices.

why.A: BIOS passwords protect access to BIOS settings but do not prevent booting from unsigned external devices.
why.C: USB settings can restrict USB ports but don't verify the trustworthiness or signature status of connected devices.
why.D: Single sign-on is an authentication method for user access and has no relation to boot device security or code signing verification.

prompt: Which of the following RAM characteristics allows for recovery from data faults in memory modules?
explanation: ECC (Error-Correcting Code) RAM has the ability to detect and correct single-bit errors that occur in memory modules during operation. It adds extra bits to data that allow the system to identify and fix corrupted data, providing fault tolerance and improving system reliability. This is the only RAM characteristic that enables recovery from data faults.

why.A: Capacity refers to the amount of memory and has nothing to do with error detection or correction capabilities.
why.B: Speed relates to how fast RAM operates and does not address data fault recovery or error correction.
why.D: DDR is a memory type designation (DDR3, DDR4, etc.) that describes the technology but not error recovery capabilities.
why.E: Parity is an older, simpler error-detection method that can only detect errors, not correct them like ECC does.
